name: Shopify
description: Shopify is an e-commerce platform. This toolkit is GraphQL-first for new Admin API automations while retaining legacy REST compatibility actions for older workflows and numeric-ID interoperability

tools.name: Accept Fulfillment Cancellation Request
tools.description: Accept a pending cancellation request as the fulfillment service managing the order. Use only for fulfillment orders assigned to this app's fulfillment service, after the merchant requests cancellation. Returns the updated fulfillment order. Uses the legacy Shopify REST Admin API and requires protected customer data access.

inputs.name: message
inputs.about: Optional reason for accepting the cancellation request.

inputs.name: fulfillment_order_id
inputs.about: ID of the fulfillment order with a pending cancellation request.

tools.name: Accept Fulfillment Request
tools.description: Accept a submitted fulfillment request as the fulfillment service managing the order. Use only for fulfillment orders assigned to this app's fulfillment service, after the merchant submits a fulfillment request. Returns the updated order, normally with request_status accepted and status in_progress. Uses the legacy Shopify REST Admin API and requires protected customer data access.

inputs.name: message
inputs.about: Optional reason for accepting the fulfillment request.

inputs.name: fulfillment_order_id
inputs.about: ID of the fulfillment order with a submitted fulfillment request.

tools.name: Activate One-Time Charge
tools.description: Activate an accepted one-time Shopify application charge to finalize billing, using the legacy activation operation. DEPRECATED: Shopify removed this endpoint as of API version 2021-01; merchant-approved charges now transition directly from pending to active without a separate activation call.

inputs.name: application_charge_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the application charge to activate. The charge must be in 'accepted' status before activation.

tools.name: Add product to custom collection (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use SHOPIFY_ADDS_A_PRODUCT_TO_A_CUSTOM_COLLECTION instead. Adds a product to an existing *custom collection*, optionally specifying its `position` if the collection is manually sorted.

inputs.name: position
inputs.about: Optional position where the product appears in a manually sorted custom collection. If unspecified, the product is added to the end. Note: Positions are not guaranteed to be consecutive. Only honored when the collection's `sort_order` is set to `manual`; ignored silently otherwise.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier for the product to add to the collection.

inputs.name: collection_id
inputs.about: The ID of the custom collection to add the product to. Note: Products can only be added to custom collections, not smart collections.

tools.name: Add product to custom collection
tools.description: Add a product to a custom collection by creating a collect resource. Use when you need to link a product to a custom collection. Note: Can only add products to custom collections, not smart collections.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier for the product to add to the collection.

inputs.name: collection_id
inputs.about: The ID of the custom collection to add the product to. Can only link products to custom collections, not smart collections.

tools.name: Adjust inventory levels
tools.description: Adjust the inventory level of an inventory item at a single location. Use when you need to increase or decrease stock quantities at a specific location.

inputs.name: location_id
inputs.about: The ID of the location where the inventory level will be adjusted. Use the Location resource to find valid location IDs.

inputs.name: inventory_item_id
inputs.about: The ID of the inventory item being adjusted. This identifies the specific product variant whose inventory will be updated.

inputs.name: available_adjustment
inputs.about: The amount to adjust the available inventory quantity. Positive values increase stock (e.g., 5 adds 5 units), negative values decrease stock (e.g., -3 removes 3 units).

tools.name: Apply fulfillment hold
tools.description: Applies a fulfillment hold to an open fulfillment order, halting all fulfillment work. Use when you need to pause fulfillment due to payment issues, fraud concerns, address problems, or inventory shortages. The fulfillment order status will change to on_hold, preventing any fulfillment work from proceeding until the hold is released.

inputs.name: reason
inputs.about: Reason for applying the hold. Must be one of: awaiting_payment, high_risk_of_fraud, incorrect_address, inventory_out_of_stock, or other.

inputs.name: reason_notes
inputs.about: Additional context or explanation for the hold reason. Provides more details beyond the standard reason.

inputs.name: notify_merchant
inputs.about: Whether to send a notification to the merchant about this hold via the Shopify mobile app. Defaults to false if not specified.

inputs.name: fulfillment_order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the fulfillment order to place on hold.

tools.name: Approve a comment
tools.description: Approves a pending comment and publishes it to a blog article, making it publicly visible to readers. This action changes the comment's status from 'pending' or 'unapproved' to 'published' and sets the published_at timestamp. Use this when moderating blog comments that require approval before appearing on the storefront. Requires the 'write_content' scope.

inputs.name: comment_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric ID of the comment to approve and publish. Must be a comment with status 'pending' or 'unapproved'. Get comment IDs from the list comments or create comment actions.

tools.name: Bulk create products via GraphQL
tools.description: Creates products using a Shopify asynchronous bulk mutation and polls for a terminal status. It returns available parsed product results or an error if results are unavailable, and may time out while the operation is still running.

inputs.name: products
inputs.about: Array of product inputs to create. Recommended 20-50+ items for optimal bulk operation efficiency.

inputs.name: max_poll_attempts
inputs.about: Maximum polling attempts before timeout. Default 60 (5 minutes with 5s interval).

inputs.name: poll_interval_seconds
inputs.about: Seconds to wait between status polls. Default 5.

tools.name: Bulk delete customer addresses (Deprecated)
tools.description: Bulk delete multiple customer addresses in a single operation. This action permanently removes several addresses from a customer's address book at once, which is more efficient than deleting addresses one by one. Use this when you need to clean up multiple invalid or outdated addresses for a customer. Requires the 'write_customers' scope and access to protected customer data.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.about: The bulk operation to perform. Currently only 'destroy' is supported, which permanently deletes the specified addresses from the customer's account.

inputs.name: address_ids
inputs.about: Array of address IDs to delete from the customer's address book. You must provide at least one address ID. Each ID should be a valid address that belongs to the specified customer.

inputs.name: customer_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the customer in Shopify.

tools.name: Delete metafields in bulk
tools.description: Deletes multiple metafields in bulk using their owner ID, namespace, and key. If a metafield doesn't exist, the mutation still succeeds but returns null for that identifier in the response.

inputs.name: metafields
inputs.about: List of metafield identifiers to delete. Each identifier specifies the owner ID (GID), namespace, and key. If a metafield doesn't exist, the mutation still succeeds but returns null for that identifier.

tools.name: Bulk delete metaobjects
tools.description: Asynchronously delete metaobjects and their associated metafields in bulk. Use this action to delete multiple metaobjects by their IDs or delete all metaobjects of a specific type. The operation is asynchronous and returns a job ID for tracking completion status.

inputs.name: where
inputs.about: Specifies which metaobjects to delete. Must provide either 'ids' (array of metaobject IDs) or 'type' (string representing metaobject type).

tools.name: Run Shopify bulk query operation
tools.description: Start a Shopify GraphQL bulk query to retrieve large datasets, such as products, orders, customers, or inventory, without manual pagination. The query must include at least one connection using the edges and node structure. Polls the current bulk operation until a terminal state or timeout, returning its metadata and any available result or partial-data URL.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: GraphQL bulk query string. CRITICAL: Every connection field (any field returning a Connection type like LineItemConnection, VariantConnection, OrderConnection, etc.) must use the edges { node { ... } } pattern. This applies to top-level queries AND all nested relationship fields (e.g., lineItems, va

inputs.name: timeout_seconds
inputs.about: Maximum number of seconds to wait for the bulk operation to complete before timing out. Shopify bulk operations can take several minutes for large datasets.

inputs.name: client_identifier
inputs.about: Optional identifier to track this bulk operation for debugging or logging purposes.

inputs.name: poll_interval_seconds
inputs.about: Number of seconds to wait between polling attempts when checking bulk operation status. Shopify recommends polling every 1-2 seconds.

tools.name: Calculate a refund
tools.description: Calculate accurate refund amounts, taxes, and transactions for a Shopify order before creating an actual refund. Use this action to: - Preview refund calculations for line items with accurate tax breakdowns - Determine shipping refund amounts and maximum refundable values - Get suggested transactions that can be used to create the actual refund The response includes transactions with kind='suggested_refund' which must be changed to kind='refund' before creating an actual refund using the create refund endpoint.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.about: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'CAD'). Required when shipping 'amount' is specified.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the order for which to calculate the refund.

inputs.name: shipping
inputs.about: Shipping refund specification. Specify either full_refund or amount, not both.

inputs.name: refund_line_items
inputs.about: Array of line items to refund. Each item requires line_item_id, quantity, and optionally restock_type with location_id for inventory management.

tools.name: Cancel App Subscription
tools.description: Cancel an app subscription in Shopify using the appSubscriptionCancel GraphQL mutation. Use when you need to cancel an existing app subscription, optionally with prorated credits.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the app subscription to be cancelled. Must be in the format: gid://shopify/AppSubscription/{id} (e.g., gid://shopify/AppSubscription/12345678).

inputs.name: prorate
inputs.about: Whether to issue prorated credits for the unused portion of the app subscription. If true, there will be a corresponding deduction (based on revenue share) to your Partner account. Defaults to false.

tools.name: Cancel Shopify bulk operation
tools.description: Cancel a running Shopify bulk operation. Use when you need to stop a long-running bulk query or mutation operation that is no longer needed. Note that there may be a short delay between when cancelation starts and when the operation is actually canceled.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the bulk operation to cancel. Must be in GID format: gid://shopify/BulkOperation/{operation_id}. You can obtain this ID from the response of bulkOperationRunQuery or bulkOperationRunMutation actions.

tools.name: Cancel a fulfillment
tools.description: Cancels an existing fulfillment by its ID, reverting all line items to an unfulfilled state. Use this when a fulfillment was created in error or needs to be redone. The cancellation is permanent and cannot be undone - the line items will return to the unfulfilled state and a new fulfillment must be created if needed. Only fulfillments that haven't been shipped or are in certain states can be cancelled.

inputs.name: fulfillment_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the fulfillment to cancel. Obtain this ID from a fulfillment that was previously created or by retrieving fulfillments for an order. The fulfillment must be in a state that allows cancellation (not already cancelled or completed with shipped status).

tools.name: Cancel a Fulfillment Order
tools.description: Cancels a fulfillment order in Shopify and marks it as closed. This creates a replacement fulfillment order with the same line items, allowing reassignment to a different location. Use this for merchant-managed fulfillments. For third-party fulfillment services, use the cancellation request endpoints instead. This endpoint immediately cancels the order without requiring acceptance from a fulfillment service.

inputs.name: fulfillment_order_id
inputs.about: The ID of the fulfillment order to cancel. Can be provided as an integer or string.

tools.name: Cancel an order
tools.description: Cancels a Shopify order and optionally restocks items and sends email notifications. Use when canceling an order that has not yet been paid or fulfilled. Orders cannot be cancelled if payment status is already paid or if the order has existing fulfillments.

inputs.name: email
inputs.about: Whether to send a cancellation email notification to the customer.

inputs.name: amount
inputs.about: The refund amount when canceling the order. Required for multi-currency orders along with currency.

inputs.name: reason
inputs.about: The reason for canceling the order. Common values include 'customer', 'fraud', 'inventory', 'declined', 'other'.

inputs.name: refund
inputs.about: An object containing detailed refund information. Should be generated using the Refund API's 'calculate' endpoint, specifying each line item with line_item_id, quantity, and restock_type.

inputs.name: restock
inputs.about: Whether to restock the items from the canceled order back into inventory. Note: This parameter is deprecated but still functional.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.about: The currency code for the refund amount (e.g., 'USD', 'CAD'). Required when amount is specified in multi-currency scenarios.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the order to cancel. Must use the order's API id, not order_number.

tools.name: Cancel Recurring Application Charge
tools.description: Cancel a recurring application charge by its ID. A successful cancellation returns an empty response. Uses the legacy REST Admin API; Shopify recommends GraphQL appSubscriptionCancel for new apps.

inputs.name: recurring_application_charge_id
inputs.about: ID of the recurring application charge to cancel.

tools.name: Close Fulfillment Order
tools.description: Mark an in-progress fulfillment order incomplete, not cancelled. Only the fulfillment service app that accepted the request can close it. The order must be assigned to a fulfillment service location with an accepted request and in_progress status. Closes the request and returns control to the merchant without cancelling the order. Uses the legacy REST Admin API.

inputs.name: message
inputs.about: Optional reason for marking the fulfillment order incomplete.

inputs.name: fulfillment_order_id
inputs.about: ID of the accepted, in-progress fulfillment order to mark incomplete.

tools.name: Close an order
tools.description: Closes an open Shopify order. Use when all line items have been fulfilled or canceled and all financial transactions are complete.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Shopify order to close. The order must be open with all line items fulfilled or canceled and all financial transactions completed.

tools.name: Complete a draft order
tools.description: Complete a draft order in Shopify and transition it to an actual order. Use when you need to finalize a draft order, reserve inventory, and create a corresponding order. When completing with payment_pending=true, the payment gateway is set to Manual.

inputs.name: draft_order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the draft order to complete.

inputs.name: payment_pending
inputs.about: When set to true, marks the order as payment pending instead of paid. If omitted, the order is marked as paid. Setting this to true will always make the payment gateway as Manual.

tools.name: Connect inventory item to location
tools.description: Connects an inventory item to a location, establishing where the item can be stocked and fulfilled. This creates an inventory level with an initial available quantity of 0. Use this when you need to enable a product variant to be stocked at a new location. After connecting, use the 'set' or 'adjust' inventory level actions to update quantities.

inputs.name: location_id
inputs.about: The ID of the location where you want to stock this inventory item. Use the 'List locations' action to retrieve available location IDs from your store.

inputs.name: inventory_item_id
inputs.about: The ID of the inventory item to connect to the location. Each product variant has an associated inventory item ID, which can be retrieved from the product variant's 'inventory_item_id' field.

inputs.name: relocate_if_necessary
inputs.about: Whether to relocate inventory from previously connected locations. Must be set to true when connecting to fulfillment service locations, since an inventory item can only be active at one fulfillment service location at a time. Defaults to false for regular locations.

tools.name: Count articles in blog
tools.description: Retrieves a count of all articles from a blog. Use when you need to know how many articles exist in a specific blog, optionally filtered by creation, publication, or update dates and publication status.

inputs.name: blog_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the blog whose articles should be counted.

inputs.name: created_at_max
inputs.about: Count only articles created at or before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

inputs.name: created_at_min
inputs.about: Count only articles created at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

inputs.name: updated_at_max
inputs.about: Count only articles last updated at or before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

inputs.name: updated_at_min
inputs.about: Count only articles last updated at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

inputs.name: published_at_max
inputs.about: Count only articles published at or before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

inputs.name: published_at_min
inputs.about: Count only articles published at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

inputs.name: published_status
inputs.about: Filter by publication status. 'published' returns only published articles, 'unpublished' returns only unpublished articles, 'any' returns all articles regardless of status. Defaults to 'any' if not specified.

tools.name: Get blogs count
tools.description: Retrieves the total count of all blogs in a Shopify store. Use this action when you need to know how many blogs exist in the store without fetching the full list of blog details. This is useful for pagination calculations, analytics, or checking if any blogs exist before performing other operations. Requires 'read_content' or 'write_content' OAuth scope.

tools.name: Retrieve count of custom collections (Deprecated)
tools.description: Retrieves a count of custom collections with optional filters. Use when you need to know how many custom collections exist in the store, optionally filtered by product, publication status, or date ranges.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: Filters count by custom collection title.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: Filters count to custom collections containing a specific product ID.

inputs.name: updated_at_max
inputs.about: Counts custom collections updated before this date (ISO 8601 format).

inputs.name: updated_at_min
inputs.about: Counts custom collections updated after this date (ISO 8601 format).

inputs.name: published_at_max
inputs.about: Counts custom collections published before this date (ISO 8601 format).

inputs.name: published_at_min
inputs.about: Counts custom collections published after this date (ISO 8601 format).

inputs.name: published_status
inputs.about: Filters count by publication status. Valid values: 'published', 'unpublished', or 'any'. Default: 'any'.

tools.name: Get draft orders count
tools.description: Retrieves a count of draft orders from a Shopify store. Use when you need to know how many draft orders exist without fetching full draft order details. Supports filtering by status and date range to count specific subsets of draft orders.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Filter draft orders by their current state. 'open': Draft orders that haven't been completed (default). 'invoice_sent': Draft orders where an invoice has been sent to the customer. 'completed': Draft orders that have been converted to actual orders.

inputs.name: updated_at_max
inputs.about: Show draft orders last modified at or before this date. Format: ISO 8601 (e.g., 2014-04-25T16:15:47-04:00).

inputs.name: updated_at_min
inputs.about: Show draft orders last modified at or after this date. Format: ISO 8601 (e.g., 2014-04-25T16:15:47-04:00).

tools.name: Count all the events (Deprecated)
tools.description: Count all events in a Shopify store with comprehensive filtering. Use when you need to determine how many events match specified criteria including date range, resource type, or action verb.

inputs.name: verb
inputs.about: Show events of a certain type/action (e.g., create, destroy, update, confirmed)

inputs.name: filter
inputs.about: Show events of certain resources, specified by a comma-separated list of resource names (e.g., Order, Product, Article, Blog, Collection, Comment, Page, PriceRule)

inputs.name: created_at_max
inputs.about: Show events created at or before this date and time. Format: ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g., 2014-04-25T16:15:47-04:00)

inputs.name: created_at_min
inputs.about: Show events created at or after this date and time. Format: ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g., 2014-04-25T16:15:47-04:00)

tools.name: Count fulfillments for order
tools.description: Retrieves a count of fulfillments associated with a specific order. Use when you need to determine how many fulfillments exist for an order, optionally filtered by creation or update dates.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier for the order whose fulfillments you want to count.

inputs.name: created_at_max
inputs.about: Filter to count fulfillments created before this date. Must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2014-04-25T16:15:47-04:00).

inputs.name: created_at_min
inputs.about: Filter to count fulfillments created after this date. Must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2014-04-25T16:15:47-04:00).

inputs.name: updated_at_max
inputs.about: Filter to count fulfillments last updated before this date. Must be in ISO 8601 format.

inputs.name: updated_at_min
inputs.about: Filter to count fulfillments last updated after this date. Must be in ISO 8601 format.

tools.name: Retrieves a count of locations (Deprecated)
tools.description: Retrieves a count of locations. Use when you need to determine how many physical or virtual locations are configured in the Shopify store.

tools.name: Count shop metafields
tools.description: Retrieves the shop-level count of metafields. Use resource-specific metafield actions for product, customer, order, collection, page, or article metafields.

tools.name: Count orders (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use SHOPIFY_RETRIEVES_AN_ORDER_COUNT instead. Retrieves the count of orders in a Shopify store. Use when you need to know how many orders exist, optionally filtered by status, dates, financial status, fulfillment status, or attribution app. Note: Only the last 60 days' worth of orders are accessible by default unless the app has been granted the read_all_orders scope.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Filter orders by their current status. Default is 'any'.

inputs.name: created_at_max
inputs.about: Count only orders created at or before this ISO 8601 datetime.

inputs.name: created_at_min
inputs.about: Count only orders created at or after this ISO 8601 datetime (e.g., '2023-03-07T00:00:00.000' or '2023-03-07 00:00:00.000').

inputs.name: updated_at_max
inputs.about: Count only orders last updated at or before this ISO 8601 datetime.

inputs.name: updated_at_min
inputs.about: Count only orders last updated at or after this ISO 8601 datetime.

inputs.name: financial_status
inputs.about: Filter orders by payment status. Note: Multiple comma-separated values do NOT work properly with the count endpoint.

inputs.name: attribution_app_id
inputs.about: Filter orders attributed to a specific app ID.

inputs.name: fulfillment_status
inputs.about: Filter orders by fulfillment state. Note: Multiple comma-separated values do NOT work properly with the count endpoint. Use 'unfulfilled' or null for unfulfilled orders.

tools.name: Retrieve page count
tools.description: Retrieve the total count of pages in a Shopify store. Use when you need to determine how many pages exist, optionally filtered by creation date, update date, publication date, publication status, or title.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: Count pages matching a specific title.

inputs.name: created_at_max
inputs.about: Filter pages created before a specified date (ISO 8601 format).

inputs.name: created_at_min
inputs.about: Filter pages created after a specified date (ISO 8601 format).

inputs.name: updated_at_max
inputs.about: Filter pages updated before a specified date (ISO 8601 format).

inputs.name: updated_at_min
inputs.about: Filter pages updated after a specified date (ISO 8601 format).

inputs.name: published_at_max
inputs.about: Filter pages published before a specified date (ISO 8601 format).

inputs.name: published_at_min
inputs.about: Filter pages published after a specified date (ISO 8601 format).

inputs.name: published_status
inputs.about: Restrict results by publication state. Valid options: 'published', 'unpublished', or 'any' (default).

tools.name: Count price rules
tools.description: Retrieves a count of all price rules. Use when you need to determine how many price rules (discount campaigns) are configured in the store.

tools.name: Count product images
tools.description: Retrieves the total count of images for a specific Shopify product. Use when you need to know how many images are associated with a product.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the Shopify product whose images are to be counted.

tools.name: Count product listings
tools.description: Count products published to your app's sales channel, not all store products. Uses the legacy REST Admin API. No query filters are supported by this endpoint.

tools.name: Retrieves a count of products
tools.description: Retrieve a count of products in the Shopify store. Use when you need to get the total number of products, optionally filtered by collection, vendor, product type, status, or date ranges.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Filter by product status (e.g., 'active', 'draft', 'archived').

inputs.name: vendor
inputs.about: Filter by vendor name (the supplier or manufacturer of the products).

inputs.name: product_type
inputs.about: Filter by product type (e.g., 'Apparel', 'Electronics', 'Footwear').

inputs.name: collection_id
inputs.about: Filter products by collection ID to count only products within a specific collection.

inputs.name: created_at_max
inputs.about: Return products created before this date. Format: ISO 8601.

inputs.name: created_at_min
inputs.about: Return products created after this date. Format: ISO 8601 (e.g., 2014-04-25T16:15:47-04:00).

inputs.name: updated_at_max
inputs.about: Return products last updated before this date. Format: ISO 8601.

inputs.name: updated_at_min
inputs.about: Return products last updated after this date. Format: ISO 8601.

inputs.name: published_at_max
inputs.about: Return products published before this date. Format: ISO 8601.

inputs.name: published_at_min
inputs.about: Return products published after this date. Format: ISO 8601.

inputs.name: published_status
inputs.about: Filter by published status (e.g., 'published', 'unpublished', 'any').

tools.name: Count product variants
tools.description: Retrieves the total count of variants for a Shopify product. Use when you need to know how many variants exist for a specific product.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the Shopify product whose variants are to be counted.

tools.name: Count script tags
tools.description: Retrieves a count of all script tags in the shop. Script tags are remote JavaScript files that are loaded into the pages of a shop's storefront or checkout. Use this action to determine the total number of script tags, optionally filtered by a specific source URL. Note: This endpoint is part of the legacy REST Admin API (deprecated). The Shopify GraphQL Admin API should be used for new integrations.

inputs.name: src
inputs.about: Filter to count only script tags with this exact source URL. If omitted, returns the total count of all script tags in the shop.

tools.name: Receive a count of all webhooks (Deprecated)
tools.description: Retrieves a count of webhook subscriptions registered to the requesting app, optionally filtered by address or topic. Subscriptions created in the Shopify admin are not accessible through the API.

inputs.name: topic
inputs.about: Filter webhook subscriptions by event topic. Valid values include 'orders/create', 'products/update', 'customers/create', etc.

inputs.name: address
inputs.about: Filter webhook subscriptions by the URI where the POST request is sent. Only counts webhooks that send to this specific address.

tools.name: Create a metafield
tools.description: Create a metafield to attach custom metadata to a supported Shopify resource, such as a product, customer, order, collection, or the shop.

inputs.name: key
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the metafield within its namespace. Must be 3-64 characters, alphanumeric, hyphen, or underscore.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The type of data stored in the metafield. Supported types include: single_line_text_field, multi_line_text_field, number_integer, number_decimal, boolean, json, rating, url, date, date_time, color, weight, volume, dimension, money, and list types.

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: The data to store in the metafield. Always stored as string format regardless of type.

inputs.name: resource
inputs.about: The type of resource to attach the metafield to. Supported resources: products, customers, blogs, collections, orders, pages, variants, articles, draft_orders, locations, product_images, smart_collections, shop.

inputs.name: namespace
inputs.about: Container for a group of metafields. Must be 3-255 characters, alphanumeric, hyphen, or underscore.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Optional description of the metafield to provide context about its purpose.

inputs.name: resource_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the resource to attach the metafield to. Not required for 'shop' resource.

tools.name: Create A New Product Image (Deprecated)
tools.description: Create a new product image for a Shopify product. Use when you need to add an image to a product by providing either an image URL or base64-encoded image data. Products can have up to 250 images in PNG, GIF, or JPG formats.

inputs.name: image
inputs.about: Object containing the image details. Must include either 'src' or 'attachment'.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the product to associate the image with.

tools.name: Create app subscription
tools.description: Create a recurring or usage-based app subscription for charging Shopify merchants. Use when setting up billing for app features and services. Returns a confirmation URL where the merchant must approve charges before the subscription becomes active.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Descriptive name for the subscription plan displayed to merchant (e.g., 'Basic Plan', 'Premium Tier').

inputs.name: test
inputs.about: Whether this is a test subscription that won't actually charge the merchant. Useful for development and testing. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: lineItems
inputs.about: One or more pricing plans defining the subscription structure. Only one pricing plan can be defined for each available type (recurring or usage-based).

inputs.name: returnUrl
inputs.about: URL where merchant is redirected after approving or declining the subscription. Should be a page in your app that handles the result.

inputs.name: trialDays
inputs.about: Number of free trial days beginning when merchant approves the subscription. Merchant won't be charged during trial period.

inputs.name: replacementBehavior
inputs.about: Controls how the new subscription interacts with existing active subscriptions.

tools.name: Create Article
tools.description: Create an article in a specific Shopify blog. A title is required.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of tags. Tags are additional short descriptors for the article.

inputs.name: image
inputs.about: Image object for an article

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The headline of the article. This field is required.

inputs.name: author
inputs.about: Name credited as the article's creator.

inputs.name: blog_id
inputs.about: The ID of the blog where the article will be created.

inputs.name: body_html
inputs.about: The text of the body of the article, complete with HTML markup.

inputs.name: published
inputs.about: Whether the article is visible. Defaults to unpublished (false) if not specified.

inputs.name: metafields
inputs.about: Custom metadata fields with key, namespace, value, and type.

inputs.name: published_at
inputs.about: Date and time (ISO 8601 format) when the article becomes visible. If not provided and published is true, the article is published immediately.

inputs.name: summary_html
inputs.about: Brief summary with HTML markup for display on other pages.

tools.name: Create Comment for Article
tools.description: Create a comment for an article in Shopify. Use when you need to add reader comments to blog articles. Requires 'content' access scope and protected customer data access.

inputs.name: ip
inputs.about: The IP address from which the comment was posted.

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: The basic Textile markup of the comment. This field is required.

inputs.name: email
inputs.about: The email address of the author of the comment. This field is required and contains protected customer data.

inputs.name: author
inputs.about: The name of the author of the comment. This field is required and contains protected customer data.

inputs.name: blog_id
inputs.about: A unique numeric identifier for the blog to which the article belongs.

inputs.name: article_id
inputs.about: A unique numeric identifier for the article to which the comment belongs.

inputs.name: user_agent
inputs.about: The browser user agent string from which the comment was posted.

tools.name: Create a new blog
tools.description: Create a new blog in Shopify. Use when you need to add a blog to the store for publishing articles and content. The title field is mandatory.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the blog. This field is required. Maximum length: 255 characters.

inputs.name: handle
inputs.about: A human-friendly unique string for the blog automatically generated from its title. If not provided, it will be auto-generated from the title.

inputs.name: metafields
inputs.about: Attaches additional metadata to a shop's resources. Each metafield object should include key, value, type, and namespace.

inputs.name: commentable
inputs.about: Whether readers can post comments to the blog and if comments are moderated or not. Defaults to 'no' if not specified.

inputs.name: template_suffix
inputs.about: The suffix of the Liquid template being used. For example, if the value is 'custom', then the blog is using the blog.custom.liquid template.

tools.name: Create carrier service
tools.description: Create a carrier service that supplies real-time shipping rates at checkout. Requires write_shipping and an eligible store: Advanced Shopify or higher, Shopify with yearly billing or the carrier service feature, or a development store that is not on the Basic plan. The callback must be a public POST endpoint. REST Admin API is legacy; new public apps must use GraphQL Admin API.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The shipping service name shown to merchants and customers.

inputs.name: active
inputs.about: Whether the service is available to serve rates at checkout. Omit to use Shopify's default.

inputs.name: format
inputs.about: Deprecated response format of the callback endpoint. Only 'json' is supported.

inputs.name: callback_url
inputs.about: Public URL of the POST endpoint where Shopify retrieves shipping rates.

inputs.name: service_discovery
inputs.about: Whether merchants can send dummy data through Shopify admin to preview shipping rates. Omit to use Shopify's default.

inputs.name: carrier_service_type
inputs.about: Deprecated property distinguishing API and legacy carrier services (for example, 'api'). Normally omit for an API-created service.

tools.name: Create checkout payment
tools.description: Create a checkout payment using an existing Shopify card-vault session. Can authorize or charge money. Requires elevated sales-channel payment processing access, protected customer data approval, and a direct payment gateway. Uses the legacy REST Admin API; the API version comes from the connection base URL. HTTP 202 means accepted, not paid: inspect transaction.status, payment_processing_error_message, and next_action for failure or authentication.

inputs.name: token
inputs.about: Token of the existing checkout: URL-safe letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.

inputs.name: amount
inputs.about: Payment amount as a decimal string, matching the checkout total.

inputs.name: session_id
inputs.about: Session ID returned by Shopify's card vault; not raw card details.

inputs.name: unique_token
inputs.about: App-generated idempotency token, unique across payment requests. Reuse only when retrying the same payment.

inputs.name: request_details
inputs.about: Customer request context required for payment processing.

tools.name: Create Country
tools.description: Create a country with tax configuration for the Shopify store. Use when you need to add a new country to the store's shipping or tax settings. **Important Notes:** - The REST Country API is deprecated as of API version 2024-07 - This action requires merchant approval for the 'write_shipping' scope - The 'tax' field is deprecated as of API version 2020-10 and custom tax values can no longer be created or updated - For new implementations, consider using the GraphQL Admin API's "Countries in shipping zone" endpoint instead

inputs.name: tax
inputs.about: The national sales tax rate applied to orders from that country in decimal format (e.g., 0.2 for 20%). Note: As of API version 2020-10, the tax field is deprecated and custom tax values can no longer be created or updated.

inputs.name: code
inputs.about: The two-letter country code in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format (e.g., 'BR' for Brazil, 'FR' for France, 'US' for United States). This is required.

tools.name: Create a custom collection
tools.description: Create a manually curated custom collection in Shopify with a required title and optional description, image, publication settings, sort order, product associations, and metafields. The returned custom collection contains its ID.

inputs.name: image
inputs.about: Image object for custom collection.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: Name of the custom collection (limit: 255 characters). This is the only required field.

inputs.name: handle
inputs.about: Human-friendly unique identifier (limit: 255 characters). Auto-generated from title if not provided. Use the returned `collection_id` for subsequent operations instead of relying on the handle.

inputs.name: collects
inputs.about: Product associations to add to the collection during creation.

inputs.name: body_html
inputs.about: HTML description displayed on collection pages.

inputs.name: published
inputs.about: Whether visible on Online Store channel. Defaults to true if not specified.

inputs.name: metafields
inputs.about: Custom metadata fields with key, value, type, and namespace.

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Product ordering method within the collection.

inputs.name: published_scope
inputs.about: Publication scope: 'web' (Online Store only) or 'global' (Online Store and Point of Sale).

inputs.name: template_suffix
inputs.about: Liquid template variant suffix for custom collection page templates.

tools.name: Create Customer
tools.description: Create a new Shopify customer with contact details, addresses, tags, and notes. Requires an email, phone number, or both first and last name.

inputs.name: note
inputs.about: An optional note about the customer.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: A comma-separated string of tags to associate with the customer.

inputs.name: email
inputs.about: The customer's unique email address. Must be unique across all customers in the store. At least one of email, phone, or (first_name and last_name) must be provided.

inputs.name: phone
inputs.about: The customer's phone number in E.164 format (e.g., +16135551212) or other dialable formats (6135551212, (613)555-1212). At least one of email, phone, or (first_name and last_name) must be provided.

inputs.name: password
inputs.about: (Deprecated) The customer's password. This field is deprecated for creating customer accounts. If provided, password_confirmation is also required.

inputs.name: addresses
inputs.about: A list of addresses for the customer.

inputs.name: last_name
inputs.about: The customer's last name. At least one of email, phone, or (first_name and last_name) must be provided.

inputs.name: first_name
inputs.about: The customer's first name. At least one of email, phone, or (first_name and last_name) must be provided.

inputs.name: verified_email
inputs.about: Whether the customer has verified their email address. Note: This is a read-only field and may be ignored by the API.

inputs.name: send_email_invite
inputs.about: If true, sends the customer an email invite to create an account.

inputs.name: send_email_welcome
inputs.about: Whether to send the customer a welcome email. When false, suppresses the welcome email. If send_email_invite is true, this can be set to false to avoid sending duplicate emails.

inputs.name: password_confirmation
inputs.about: (Deprecated) Confirmation of the customer's password. This field is deprecated for creating customer accounts. Required if password is provided.

tools.name: Generate Customer Account Activation URL
tools.description: Generate a one-time account activation URL for a customer whose account is in 'disabled' state (not yet activated). Use this when you've imported customers and need activation URLs to send in welcome emails. The URL allows customers to set their password and activate their account. Each URL expires after 30 days. Generating a new URL invalidates any previously generated URL for that customer.

inputs.name: customer_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the customer whose account activation URL needs to be generated.

tools.name: Create customer address
tools.description: Create a new address for a customer. Use when you need to add an address to an existing customer's address list.

inputs.name: address
inputs.about: The address information to be created for the customer.

inputs.name: customer_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the customer to whom the address will be added.

tools.name: Create delegate access token
tools.description: Create a delegate access token with a subset of the parent token's permissions. Use when you need to securely delegate limited access to subsystems or services. Each delegate token inherits only the specified scopes, ensuring minimal required permissions rather than full app access. Note: Delegate tokens cannot create new delegate tokens.

inputs.name: expires_in
inputs.about: Token expiration time in seconds from creation. If not specified, the delegate token expires when the parent token expires. Maximum value depends on parent token lifetime.

inputs.name: delegate_access_scope
inputs.about: Array of access scopes to delegate (must be subset of parent token scopes). Each scope defines specific permissions like 'read_products', 'write_orders'. The app can only delegate scopes it was originally granted.

tools.name: Create Discount Code
tools.description: Creates a discount code for an existing price rule. Price rules define the discount logic (e.g., 10% off, buy X get Y), and discount codes are the actual codes (e.g., 'SUMMER10') customers enter at checkout. Important: The price rule must exist before creating a discount code - use a price rule creation action first if needed. Each price rule can have multiple discount codes associated with it. Use this when you need to generate customer-facing discount codes for an established discount promotion.

inputs.name: code
inputs.about: The case-insensitive discount code that customers enter at checkout. Must be unique across your store. Maximum 255 characters. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores. Examples: 'SUMMER10', 'WELCOME2024', 'FREESHIP'.

inputs.name: price_rule_id
inputs.about: The ID of the price rule that the discount code will belong to. This price rule must already exist in your Shopify store and defines the discount logic (amount, eligibility, duration, etc.). You can get price rule IDs by listing price rules or creating a new one.

tools.name: Create Discount Codes Batch
tools.description: Create a discount code creation job for batch processing. Use when you need to asynchronously create up to 100 discount codes for a price rule in a single request.

inputs.name: price_rule_id
inputs.about: The ID of the price rule that the discount codes will belong to.

inputs.name: discount_codes
inputs.about: Array of discount code objects to create. Maximum 100 codes can be created in a single batch request.

tools.name: Create a new draft order
tools.description: Create a draft order in Shopify. Use when you need to create orders in draft state using product variant line items or custom line items. Draft orders are useful for creating orders on behalf of customers, generating invoices, or reserving inventory.

inputs.name: note
inputs.about: Merchant note about the draft order.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: Comma-separated tags.

inputs.name: email
inputs.about: Customer's email address.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.about: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.

inputs.name: line_items
inputs.about: Array of line item objects. At least one line item is required. Each line item must have a quantity, and either a variant_id (for product variants) or title and price (for custom items).

inputs.name: tax_exempt
inputs.about: Whether the customer is exempt from taxes.

inputs.name: customer_id
inputs.about: ID of an existing customer to associate with the draft order.

inputs.name: shipping_line
inputs.about: Shipping line for draft order.

inputs.name: billing_address
inputs.about: Billing address for draft order.

inputs.name: note_attributes
inputs.about: Custom name/value pairs for additional information.

inputs.name: applied_discount
inputs.about: Applied discount with title, description, value, value_type (either 'fixed_amount' or 'percentage'), and amount.

inputs.name: shipping_address
inputs.about: Shipping address for draft order.

inputs.name: use_customer_default_address
inputs.about: Whether to load customer's default shipping address (default: false).

tools.name: Create EventBridge webhook subscription
tools.description: Create an AWS EventBridge webhook subscription in Shopify. Use when you need to configure real-time event notifications to AWS EventBridge for events like order creation, product updates, or customer changes. EventBridge webhooks push events to your AWS partner event source immediately when changes occur, eliminating polling. You can filter events and control payload fields to optimize performance.

inputs.name: topic
inputs.about: The event type that triggers the webhook. Choose from available Shopify webhook topics like ORDERS_CREATE, PRODUCTS_UPDATE, CUSTOMERS_CREATE, etc.

inputs.name: webhook_subscription
inputs.about: Configuration details for the EventBridge webhook subscription including ARN, format, and optional filters.

tools.name: Create Fulfillment
tools.description: Creates a fulfillment for one or many fulfillment orders for a specific order. This completes the shipping process by marking items as fulfilled. IMPORTANT: You must first retrieve fulfillment orders using a "Get fulfillment orders for order" action to obtain the fulfillment_order_id and line item IDs needed for this action. Use when: You need to mark order items as shipped/fulfilled for orders assigned to merchant-managed locations or third-party fulfillment services. Note: As of API version 2024-10, fulfillments can only be created for merchant-managed locations or third-party fulfillment services owned by your app.

inputs.name: message
inputs.about: A message associated with the fulfillment. Only available if the fulfillment order is assigned to a third-party fulfillment service.

inputs.name: tracking_info
inputs.about: Tracking information for the shipment.

inputs.name: origin_address
inputs.about: The address of the fulfillment location, intended for tax purposes.

inputs.name: notify_customer
inputs.about: Whether to send a notification to the customer about this fulfillment. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: line_items_by_fulfillment_order
inputs.about: Array of fulfillment orders and their line items to fulfill. At least one fulfillment order is required.

tools.name: Create Fulfillment Event
tools.description: Creates a tracking event for a fulfillment to update shipment status. These events appear on the customer's order status page to track delivery progress (e.g., "in_transit", "out_for_delivery", "delivered"). Use this to provide real-time tracking updates from shipping carriers. Requires an existing fulfillment - use after creating a fulfillment for an order.

inputs.name: zip
inputs.about: Postal/zip code of the event location.

inputs.name: city
inputs.about: City of the event location.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: The status of the fulfillment event. Valid values: attempted_delivery (delivery was attempted), carrier_picked_up (picked up by carrier), confirmed (fulfillment confirmed), delayed (delayed), delivered (successfully delivered), failure (fulfillment request failed), in_transit (shipment in transit),

inputs.name: country
inputs.about: Country of the event location.

inputs.name: message
inputs.about: An arbitrary message describing the status, can be provided by shipping carrier.

inputs.name: address1
inputs.about: Street address of the event location.

inputs.name: latitude
inputs.about: Geographic latitude coordinate.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The ID of the order associated with the fulfillment.

inputs.name: province
inputs.about: Province/state of the event location.

inputs.name: longitude
inputs.about: Geographic longitude coordinate.

inputs.name: happened_at
inputs.about: The date and time when the fulfillment event occurred (ISO 8601 format).

inputs.name: fulfillment_id
inputs.about: The ID of the fulfillment to create an event for.

tools.name: Create Fulfillment Service
tools.description: Register a fulfillment service and automatically create its associated location. Use for a warehouse that prepares and ships orders on behalf of the merchant. Requires write_fulfillments. The callback prefix must host fulfillment-order notifications; tracking and stock callbacks depend on their respective flags. REST Admin API is legacy; new public apps must use GraphQL Admin API.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The fulfillment service name shown to merchants.

inputs.name: callback_url
inputs.about: Required public URL prefix for fulfillment_order_notification, fetch_tracking_numbers and fetch_stock callbacks. Shopify must accept the callback host.

inputs.name: tracking_support
inputs.about: Whether Shopify retrieves tracking numbers from the service. Omit to use Shopify's default.

inputs.name: inventory_management
inputs.about: Whether the service tracks inventory and supplies stock updates. Omit to use Shopify's default.

inputs.name: requires_shipping_method
inputs.about: Deprecated: whether products require physical shipping. Omit to use Shopify's default.

inputs.name: fulfillment_orders_opt_in
inputs.about: Deprecated; Shopify defaults to true in 2026-04 and recommends omitting this field. Functioning services must use the fulfillment-order workflow.

tools.name: Create Gift Card
tools.description: Create a gift card for a Shopify store. Use when you need to issue a new gift card with a specified value. Requires write_gift_cards access scope. Gift card codes can only be retrieved at creation time.

inputs.name: gift_card
inputs.about: The gift card object containing all necessary information to create a gift card.

tools.name: Create Marketing Event Engagements
tools.description: Create engagement data for a marketing event in Shopify. Use when tracking customer interactions like views, clicks, and ad spend on marketing events before customers reach the website.

inputs.name: engagements
inputs.about: A list of engagement objects containing customer activity data. At least one engagement is required.

inputs.name: marketing_event_id
inputs.about: The ID of the marketing event to add engagements to.

tools.name: Create Marketing Event
tools.description: Create a marketing event in Shopify to track promotional actions. Use when you need to track marketing campaigns targeting customers across various channels.

inputs.name: paid
inputs.about: Indicates whether the promotion is paid or organic. Defaults to false if not specified.

inputs.name: budget
inputs.about: Campaign budget amount as a decimal string. If specified, currency and budget_type are also required.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.about: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code. Required if budget is specified.

inputs.name: ended_at
inputs.about: Actual campaign end time in ISO 8601 format.

inputs.name: remote_id
inputs.about: External identifier for this marketing event. Used for validation of engagement data.

inputs.name: event_type
inputs.about: Type of marketing event. Valid values: ad, post, message, retargeting, transactional, affiliate, loyalty, newsletter, or abandoned_cart.

inputs.name: manage_url
inputs.about: URL where the campaign can be managed or edited.

inputs.name: started_at
inputs.about: The date and time when the marketing action started, in ISO 8601 format.

inputs.name: utm_medium
inputs.about: Optional UTM parameter for medium type.

inputs.name: utm_source
inputs.about: Optional UTM parameter for traffic source.

inputs.name: budget_type
inputs.about: Budget type. Valid values: daily or lifetime. Required if budget is specified.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Campaign details or description.

inputs.name: preview_url
inputs.about: URL where the campaign content can be previewed.

inputs.name: utm_campaign
inputs.about: Optional UTM parameter for campaign identification.

inputs.name: referring_domain
inputs.about: Destination domain. Required if marketing_channel is 'search' or 'social'.

inputs.name: marketing_channel
inputs.about: Distribution channel for the marketing event. Valid values: search, display, social, email, referral, chat, or receipt.

inputs.name: marketed_resources
inputs.about: Array of resources (products, collections, etc.) being marketed in this campaign.

inputs.name: scheduled_to_end_at
inputs.about: Planned campaign end time in ISO 8601 format.

tools.name: Create blog metafield
tools.description: Creates a new metafield for a Shopify blog. Metafields store additional custom information (metadata) on blog resources such as sponsor names, SEO keywords, publication dates, or custom attributes not included in standard blog fields.

inputs.name: key
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the metafield within its namespace. Must be 3-64 characters, alphanumeric, hyphen, or underscore.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The type of data stored in the metafield. Supported types include: single_line_text_field, multi_line_text_field, number_integer, number_decimal, boolean, json, rating, url, date, date_time, color, weight, volume, dimension, money, and list types.

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: The data to store in the metafield. Always stored as string format regardless of type.

inputs.name: blog_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the blog resource to create a metafield for.

inputs.name: namespace
inputs.about: Container for a group of metafields. Must be 3-255 characters, alphanumeric, hyphen, or underscore.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Optional description of the metafield to provide context about its purpose.

tools.name: Create Mobile Platform Application
tools.description: Create an iOS or Android mobile platform application associated with the app. Configures universal/app links, iOS shared web credentials, or App Clips. Use only application identifiers you control. Shopify Support must enable the mobile_platform_applications scope. Shared web credentials require a custom domain. REST Admin API is legacy; new public apps must use GraphQL Admin API.

inputs.name: platform
inputs.about: Mobile application platform: ios or android.

inputs.name: application_id
inputs.about: iOS App ID (team ID and bundle ID) or Android application ID.

inputs.name: enabled_app_clips
inputs.about: Whether to support iOS App Clips.

inputs.name: app_clip_application_id
inputs.about: iOS App ID of the app clip; may be null when unused.

inputs.name: sha256_cert_fingerprints
inputs.about: SHA256 fingerprints of the app signing certificate; Android only.

inputs.name: enabled_shared_webcredentials
inputs.about: Whether to support iOS shared web credentials; requires a custom domain.

inputs.name: enabled_universal_or_app_links
inputs.about: Whether URLs can link directly to the iOS or Android app.

tools.name: Create One-Time Application Charge
tools.description: Create a new one-time application charge in Shopify. Use when you need to bill merchants for one-time features, upgrades, or services. After creation, the merchant must approve the charge via the confirmation_url before it becomes active.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the application charge shown to merchants during approval. Must be descriptive and clear about what the charge is for.

inputs.name: test
inputs.about: Whether this is a test charge. Test charges do not result in actual credit card charges and are useful for development. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: price
inputs.about: The price of the application charge. Must be between 0.50 and 10,000.00 in the shop's currency.

inputs.name: return_url
inputs.about: The URL where the merchant is redirected after accepting or declining the charge. Shopify appends charge_id and status parameters to this URL.

tools.name: Create an order
tools.description: Create a fully committed (real) order in Shopify without payment processing. Use when programmatically generating orders with line items, customer information, and addresses. Creates a live order immediately — not a draft; use draftOrderCreate for draft workflows.

inputs.name: note
inputs.about: Additional order notes for internal use.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of tags for order organization.

inputs.name: email
inputs.about: Customer's email address. Used for order notifications.

inputs.name: phone
inputs.about: Customer phone number for SMS notifications.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.about: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code.

inputs.name: customer
inputs.about: Customer information. Can reference existing customer by id or create new with first_name, last_name, email fields.

inputs.name: total_tax
inputs.about: Sum of all tax line amounts in shop currency.

inputs.name: line_items
inputs.about: Collection of items being purchased. Each line item should include at minimum: title, price, grams, quantity, and taxable. Can also include variant_id or product_id for existing products.

inputs.name: send_receipt
inputs.about: Whether to email order confirmation to customer. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: transactions
inputs.about: Transaction objects representing payment information. Each includes kind, amount, status, and optionally gateway.

inputs.name: discount_codes
inputs.about: Discount codes to apply. Note: Only the first code is applied when creating an order.

inputs.name: shipping_lines
inputs.about: Shipping method details. Each should include title and price.

inputs.name: billing_address
inputs.about: Mailing address for billing or shipping.

inputs.name: financial_status
inputs.about: Payment state of the order. Can only be set when the order is created. Valid values: pending, authorized, partially_paid, paid, partially_refunded, refunded, voided.

inputs.name: shipping_address
inputs.about: Mailing address for billing or shipping.

inputs.name: fulfillment_status
inputs.about: Order completion state. Valid values: fulfilled, partial, restocked, or null.

inputs.name: inventory_behaviour
inputs.about: Controls inventory claiming. Valid values: bypass (default, no inventory claimed), decrement_ignoring_policy (claim inventory regardless of policy), decrement_obeying_policy (claim inventory respecting policy).

inputs.name: send_fulfillment_receipt
inputs.about: Whether to email shipping confirmation to customer. Defaults to false.

tools.name: Create order risk
tools.description: Creates a risk assessment record for a Shopify order, documenting fraud detection findings or security concerns. Use this to record risk evaluations from external fraud detection systems or internal risk analysis tools. **Important:** This REST API endpoint is deprecated as of API version 2025-10. For new implementations, use the GraphQL orderRiskAssessmentCreate mutation instead. See: https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/mutations/orderRiskAssessmentCreate **Common use cases:** - Recording fraud detection results from third-party services (e.g., MaxMind, Sift, Signifyd) - Documenting manual fraud reviews - Flagging high-risk orders for merchant review

inputs.name: score
inputs.about: Numeric risk score as a string, ranging from 0.0 (lowest risk) to 1.0 (highest risk). Higher values indicate greater fraud likelihood.

inputs.name: source
inputs.about: Identifier for the source or system that generated this risk assessment (e.g., fraud detection service name, internal system identifier).

inputs.name: display
inputs.about: If true, this risk assessment will be visible on the order details page and will influence Shopify's overall order risk level calculation. Cannot be changed after creation. Set to false for internal-only assessments.

inputs.name: message
inputs.about: Detailed explanation of the fraud check results that will be displayed to the merchant on the order details page (only visible when display is set to true).

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the order to create a risk assessment for.

inputs.name: cause_cancel
inputs.about: If true, indicates this risk assessment is severe enough to warrant automatic order cancellation. Use true for high-risk orders that should not be fulfilled.

inputs.name: recommendation
inputs.about: Suggested action: 'cancel' (high risk), 'investigate' (medium risk), or 'accept' (low risk).

tools.name: Create transaction for order
tools.description: Creates an order transaction for authorization, capture, refund, void, or sale. Capture, void, and refund require a parent transaction ID; for multi-currency orders, currency is required for refund and capture transactions.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.about: The transaction type. Valid values: 'authorization' (reserve amount), 'capture' (transfer reserved money, requires parent_id), 'sale' (authorization + capture in one step), 'void' (cancel pending authorization/capture), 'refund' (return captured money to customer).

inputs.name: test
inputs.about: Whether the transaction is a test transaction.

inputs.name: amount
inputs.about: The amount of money included in the transaction. If not provided, defaults to the total cost of the order. For multi-currency orders, this field is required when creating refund and capture transactions.

inputs.name: gateway
inputs.about: The name of the payment gateway through which the transaction is issued.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.about: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the transaction. Required for multi-currency orders when creating refund and capture transactions.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The ID of the order for which the transaction is being created.

inputs.name: parent_id
inputs.about: The ID of an associated transaction. Required for capture, void, and refund operations to link to the original authorization. Not required for authorization or sale.

inputs.name: source_name
inputs.about: The origin channel of the transaction (e.g., 'web', 'pos').

inputs.name: authorization
inputs.about: The authorization code associated with the transaction.

tools.name: Create a new page
tools.description: Create a static web page in Shopify. Use when you need to add long-term static content like About Us, Contact, or Privacy Policy pages. The title and body_html fields are required.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The page heading. This field is required; omitting it returns a 422 error.

inputs.name: author
inputs.about: Name of the person who created the page.

inputs.name: handle
inputs.about: Human-friendly URL identifier used by Liquid templating. Must be unique across all pages in the store - if a page with this handle already exists, the API will reject the request with a 422 error. To avoid conflicts, omit this field to let Shopify auto-generate a unique handle from the title.

inputs.name: body_html
inputs.about: Optional HTML content of the page, including markup tags.

inputs.name: published
inputs.about: Publication status. Defaults to true (published); set to false for unpublished pages.

inputs.name: metafields
inputs.about: Additional metadata fields with key, namespace, value, and type.

inputs.name: published_at
inputs.about: When the page was published in ISO 8601 datetime format; null when hidden.

inputs.name: template_suffix
inputs.about: Suffix determining which template renders the page; null uses default template.

tools.name: Create Price Rule
tools.description: Creates a price rule that defines discount logic for Shopify orders. Price rules specify how discounts work (percentage/fixed amount off, which products, which customers, etc.) and can be associated with discount codes for use at checkout. Common use cases: - Percentage off all products (e.g., 20% off sitewide) - Fixed amount off orders (e.g., $10 off orders over $50) - Buy X Get Y (BXGY) discounts - Free shipping offers - Customer segment-specific discounts Note: After creating a price rule, use the discount code creation endpoint to generate codes that customers can apply.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the price rule for internal use in Shopify admin. This is NOT the discount code customers enter - codes are created separately. Use descriptive names like 'Summer Sale 2026' or 'BXGY Shirts'.

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: The discount amount as a negative string. For percentage discounts: '-20.0' means 20% off. For fixed_amount discounts: '-10.0' means $10 off. For free shipping (shipping_line target_type), must be exactly '-100' (100% off).

inputs.name: ends_at
inputs.about: When the discount expires, in ISO 8601 format. Must be after starts_at. If omitted, the discount never expires (remains active indefinitely). Format: 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

inputs.name: starts_at
inputs.about: When the discount becomes active, in ISO 8601 format. Use UTC timezone (Z suffix) or include timezone offset. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ' or 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM'.

inputs.name: value_type
inputs.about: The type of discount. Use 'fixed_amount' for a dollar amount off or 'percentage' for a percentage off. For shipping_line target_type, only 'percentage' is accepted.

inputs.name: target_type
inputs.about: What the discount applies to. Use 'line_item' for product discounts or 'shipping_line' for shipping discounts.

inputs.name: usage_limit
inputs.about: Maximum total number of times any discount code associated with this price rule can be used across all customers. If omitted, unlimited usage. Example: 100 means the discount can be used 100 times total.

inputs.name: allocation_limit
inputs.about: Number of times the discount can be allocated on a single cart. Only valid for BXGY discounts.

inputs.name: target_selection
inputs.about: Which items the discount applies to. Use 'all' for all items or 'entitled' for specific products/collections/variants.

inputs.name: allocation_method
inputs.about: How the discount is allocated. Use 'each' to apply the discount to each eligible item or 'across' to split the discount across all items. IMPORTANT: Must be 'across' when target_selection is 'all'. Must be 'each' when target_type is 'shipping_line'.

inputs.name: once_per_customer
inputs.about: If true, each customer can only use this discount once (tracked by customer account). If false or omitted, customers can use it multiple times. Useful for new customer offers or preventing abuse.

inputs.name: customer_selection
inputs.about: Which customers the discount applies to. Use 'all' for all customers or 'prerequisite' for specific customer segments or IDs.

inputs.name: entitled_country_ids
inputs.about: Country IDs eligible for shipping discounts. Only valid when target_type is 'shipping_line'.

inputs.name: entitled_product_ids
inputs.about: Product IDs eligible for the discount. Only valid when target_type is 'line_item' and target_selection is 'entitled'.

inputs.name: entitled_variant_ids
inputs.about: Variant IDs eligible for the discount. Only valid when target_type is 'line_item' and target_selection is 'entitled'. Cannot include variants of products in entitled_product_ids.

inputs.name: entitled_collection_ids
inputs.about: Collection IDs eligible for the discount. Only valid when target_type is 'line_item' and target_selection is 'entitled'.

inputs.name: prerequisite_product_ids
inputs.about: Product IDs required in the cart for Buy X Get Y discounts.

inputs.name: prerequisite_variant_ids
inputs.about: Variant IDs required in the cart for Buy X Get Y discounts.

inputs.name: prerequisite_customer_ids
inputs.about: Specific customer IDs required for the discount to apply. Cannot be used with customer_segment_prerequisite_ids.

inputs.name: prerequisite_collection_ids
inputs.about: Collection IDs required in the cart for the discount to apply.

inputs.name: prerequisite_quantity_range
inputs.about: Minimum item quantity required for the discount to apply. Cannot be combined with prerequisite_to_entitlement_quantity_ratio.

inputs.name: prerequisite_subtotal_range
inputs.about: Minimum order subtotal required for the discount to apply. Cannot be combined with prerequisite_to_entitlement_quantity_ratio.

inputs.name: customer_segment_prerequisite_ids
inputs.about: Customer segment IDs required for the discount to apply. Cannot be used with prerequisite_customer_ids.

inputs.name: prerequisite_shipping_price_range
inputs.about: Maximum shipping price requirement for the discount to apply. Cannot be combined with prerequisite_to_entitlement_quantity_ratio.

inputs.name: prerequisite_to_entitlement_quantity_ratio
inputs.about: Buy/Get ratio for BXGY (Buy X Get Y) discounts. Cannot be combined with prerequisite_subtotal_range, prerequisite_quantity_range, or prerequisite_shipping_price_range.

tools.name: Create a product (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use SHOPIFY_CREATES_A_NEW_PRODUCT instead. Creates a new product in a Shopify store; a product title is generally required. Note: The Product REST API is deprecated as of API version 2025-10. While it continues to function, Shopify recommends migrating to the GraphQL Admin API for product management in new implementations. Inventory Management: inventory_quantity is read-only and cannot be set during product creation. To manage inventory, first create the product, then use the InventoryLevel resource with the variant's inventory_item_id (returned in the response) to adjust quantities at specific locations. Response: product data nested at `data.response_data.product`; extract `id` and `variants[0].id` for subsequent image or collection calls.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of the product. Shopify requires this field when creating a product.

inputs.name: vendor
inputs.about: The name of the product's vendor or manufacturer.

inputs.name: variants
inputs.about: Array of product variants. If not provided, Shopify creates a default variant Start with only `price` and add attributes incrementally — complex payloads cause 400/422 errors. Deduplicate SKUs and ensure valid handles before calling; duplicate SKUs or missing required variant fields trigger 422 vali

inputs.name: body_html
inputs.about: A detailed description of the product, which can include HTML formatting for rich text.

inputs.name: product_type
inputs.about: A category for the product, used for filtering and organizing products in Shopify.

tools.name: Create Product Image (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use SHOPIFY_CREATE_A_NEW_PRODUCT_IMAGE instead. Creates a new product image for a Shopify product. Use this tool to add images to products either by providing a publicly accessible image URL (src) or by uploading base64-encoded image data (attachment). You can specify the image position (1 is the main image), add alt text for accessibility, and associate the image with specific product variants. Supports PNG, JPG, and GIF formats. Products can have up to 250 images.

inputs.name: image
inputs.about: An object containing the image details including source URL or attachment data, optional position, alt text, and variant associations. `src` must be a direct, publicly accessible HTTPS URL (no redirects, no HTML responses, no internal/temporary links); file size must be under ~20 MB.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier of the Shopify product to add the image to. Must be a valid product ID from your store. When chaining with other Shopify calls, extract from `data.response_data.product.id` in prior responses.

tools.name: Create product metafield
tools.description: Creates a new metafield for a specific Shopify product. Each namespace+key combination must be unique per product; use the update action if the metafield already exists.

inputs.name: key
inputs.about: The key for the metafield. Must be at least 3 characters long.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The value type of the metafield. Defaults to single_line_text_field.

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: The value for the metafield.

inputs.name: namespace
inputs.about: The namespace for the metafield. Must be at least 3 characters long.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Shopify product to add a metafield to.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A description of the information that the metafield contains.

tools.name: Create Product Resource Feedback
tools.description: Submit feedback for a product, replacing this app's previous feedback. Requires a Sales Channel app. Use requires_action for merchant-facing product issues, or success without messages to clear them. Outdated feedback can return 409. REST Admin API is legacy; new public apps must use GraphQL bulkProductResourceFeedbackCreate instead.

inputs.name: state
inputs.about: requires_action reports product issues; success removes prior feedback.

inputs.name: messages
inputs.about: Required for requires_action; omit for success. One to ten messages, each at most 100 characters, starting with a capital letter (not all caps) and ending with a period.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: ID of the product receiving feedback.

inputs.name: resource_updated_at
inputs.about: Forward the product's updated_at timestamp unchanged for feedback ordering.

inputs.name: feedback_generated_at
inputs.about: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this payload was constructed, not when queued feedback is delivered.

tools.name: Create a new product variant
tools.description: Create a new product variant for an existing product. Use when adding a new variant with specific option values (like size, color). Each product can have up to 3 options and 100 variants maximum.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.about: The variant object containing variant details

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The ID of the product to create the variant for

tools.name: Create Pub/Sub webhook subscription
tools.description: Create a Google Cloud Pub/Sub webhook subscription in Shopify. Use when you need to configure real-time event notifications to Google Cloud Pub/Sub for events like order creation, product updates, or customer changes. Pub/Sub webhooks push events to your GCP topic immediately when changes occur, eliminating polling. You can filter events and control payload fields to optimize performance.

inputs.name: topic
inputs.about: The event type that triggers the webhook. Choose from available Shopify webhook topics like ORDERS_CREATE, PRODUCTS_UPDATE, CUSTOMERS_CREATE, etc.

inputs.name: webhook_subscription
inputs.about: Configuration details for the Pub/Sub webhook subscription including GCP project, topic, format, and optional filters.

tools.name: Create recurring application charge
tools.description: Create a fixed-price, 30-day recurring app charge, optionally with usage billing. The merchant must approve confirmation_url before billing starts. Set test=true for testing without credit-card charges. Activating a new charge replaces the app's existing recurring charge. REST Admin API is legacy; new public apps must use GraphQL Admin API instead.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The recurring charge name shown to the merchant.

inputs.name: test
inputs.about: Set true to prevent credit-card billing. Null represents a non-test charge; omit to use Shopify's default.

inputs.name: price
inputs.about: The fixed recurring price, maximum 10,000. Zero supports usage-only billing.

inputs.name: terms
inputs.about: Usage-based billing terms presented to the merchant. Required with capped_amount.

inputs.name: return_url
inputs.about: Valid URL where Shopify redirects the merchant after accepting the charge.

inputs.name: trial_days
inputs.about: Number of free-trial days, starting when the charge is activated.

inputs.name: capped_amount
inputs.about: Maximum usage-based amount per billing cycle. Requires terms when provided.

tools.name: Create Redirect
