tools.description: Create a URL redirect in Shopify. Use when you need to redirect an old path to a new location. When a full URL is provided as the path, it will be saved as an absolute path without the domain.

inputs.name: path
inputs.about: The old path to be redirected. When the user visits this path, they will be redirected to the target. Maximum 1024 characters. When a full URL is provided, it will be saved as an absolute path without the domain.

inputs.name: target
inputs.about: The target location where the user will be redirected. Can be set to any path on the shop's site or to an external URL. Maximum 255 characters.

tools.name: Create order refund
tools.description: Creates a refund for a Shopify order with line items, shipping, or transactions. Multi-currency orders require currency; development or trial stores are limited to 5 refunds per minute.

inputs.name: note
inputs.about: An optional note attached to the refund explaining the reason.

inputs.name: notify
inputs.about: Whether to send a refund notification email to the customer. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.about: The three-letter currency code (ISO 4217 format) for the entire refund. Required for multi-currency orders. This is separate from the currency field in individual transactions.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the order to refund.

inputs.name: shipping
inputs.about: Shipping refund details.

inputs.name: transactions
inputs.about: Optional list of refund transactions obtained from the calculate endpoint (with kind changed from 'suggested_refund' to 'refund').

inputs.name: refund_line_items
inputs.about: List of line items to refund. Each line item must include line_item_id, quantity, and restock_type.

inputs.name: discrepancy_reason
inputs.about: The reason for any discrepancy between calculated and actual refund amounts.

tools.name: Create Resource Feedback
tools.description: Creates shop-level resource feedback to notify Shopify merchants about app setup requirements or successful configuration. Feedback appears on the merchant's admin home screen. Each new submission automatically replaces previous feedback. Use state='requires_action' to alert merchants about mandatory setup steps, or state='success' to confirm proper configuration.

inputs.name: state
inputs.about: Indicates whether merchant action is needed. Must be 'requires_action' or 'success'.

inputs.name: messages
inputs.about: Array with exactly one message string (max 100 chars). Required when state is 'requires_action', disallowed when state is 'success'. Message should follow format: '[Problem explanation]. [Suggested action].'

inputs.name: feedback_generated_at
inputs.about: ISO 8601 UTC DateTime when feedback was generated (e.g., '2024-04-01T18:56:53.423703Z').

tools.name: Create a new product (Deprecated)
tools.description: Create a new product in Shopify. Use when you need to add a new product to the store with details like title, description, variants, options, and images.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: Comma-separated tags for filtering and search (max 250 tags, 255 chars each)

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The name of the product (required)

inputs.name: images
inputs.about: Array of product images

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Product status: 'active' (published and visible), 'archived' (hidden), or 'draft' (unpublished)

inputs.name: vendor
inputs.about: The name of the product's vendor or manufacturer

inputs.name: options
inputs.about: Array of product options (max 3 options, e.g., Color, Size). Required if variants use option1/option2/option3

inputs.name: variants
inputs.about: Array of product variants. If not provided, Shopify creates a default variant

inputs.name: body_html
inputs.about: Product description supporting HTML formatting

inputs.name: published
inputs.about: Whether to publish the product immediately

inputs.name: metafields
inputs.about: Custom metadata fields (e.g., for SEO: use namespace='global', key='title_tag' or 'description_tag')

inputs.name: product_type
inputs.about: Categorization for filtering and searching (e.g., 'Snowboard', 'Apparel')

inputs.name: template_suffix
inputs.about: Liquid template suffix for custom product pages

tools.name: Create Script Tag
tools.description: Create a new script tag in Shopify to load remote JavaScript into your online store. Script tags allow you to add custom functionality to your storefront by loading external JavaScript files. Requires 'write_script_tags' OAuth scope. Note: As of February 1, 2025, creating script tags for order status pages is blocked by Shopify. Use 'online_store' display_scope for storefront functionality.

inputs.name: src
inputs.about: URL of the remote script to load. Must be HTTPS.

inputs.name: cache
inputs.about: Whether the script should be cached by the CDN. Default: false.

inputs.name: event
inputs.about: DOM event that triggers the script load. Must be 'onload' (the only supported value).

inputs.name: display_scope
inputs.about: Where the script displays. Options: 'online_store' (storefront only), 'order_status' (order status page - restricted since Feb 2025), or 'all' (both). Defaults to 'online_store' (recommended).

tools.name: Create Smart Collection
tools.description: Create a new smart collection with automated product rules. Use when you need to create dynamic collections that automatically include products matching specific criteria (e.g., by vendor, price range, tags). Requires write_products scope.

inputs.name: image
inputs.about: Image object for smart collection.

inputs.name: rules
inputs.about: Array of rule objects defining which products are automatically included in this collection. Products must match all rules (or any rule if disjunctive is true).

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: Collection name, maximum 255 characters. This is the display name shown to customers.

inputs.name: body_html
inputs.about: HTML description displayed on collection pages. Can include formatting and markup.

inputs.name: published
inputs.about: Publishing status of the collection. Defaults to true (published).

inputs.name: sort_order
inputs.about: Product ordering method within the collection. Defaults to 'best-selling' if not specified.

inputs.name: disjunctive
inputs.about: If true, products match ANY rule; if false (default), products must match ALL rules.

inputs.name: template_suffix
inputs.about: Liquid template suffix for custom styling. If 'custom', uses collection.custom.liquid template.

tools.name: Create or Update Theme Asset
tools.description: Creates or updates a theme asset file (templates, stylesheets, scripts, or images) within a Shopify theme. This action uploads or modifies files in the theme's file structure. For text-based files (HTML, Liquid, CSS, JS), use the 'value' parameter with file content. For binary files (images), use 'attachment' with base64-encoded data or 'src' with an external URL. To duplicate an existing asset, use 'source_key'. **Important**: Exactly one of value, attachment, src, or source_key must be provided per request. **Requirements**: - Requires 'write_themes' scope with merchant approval - Note: REST Admin API is legacy as of October 2024; new apps should use GraphQL Admin API from April 2025

inputs.name: key
inputs.about: The file path within the theme, consisting of directory and filename. Must follow the theme directory structure (e.g., 'assets/' for CSS/JS/images, 'templates/' for page templates, 'layout/' for layout files, 'sections/' for theme sections, 'snippets/' for reusable code, 'config/' for theme settings

inputs.name: src
inputs.about: A publicly accessible URL from which Shopify will download the asset file. Typically used for images or other binary assets hosted externally. Shopify will fetch and store the file from this URL. **Constraint**: Exactly one of value, attachment, src, or source_key must be provided.

inputs.name: value
inputs.about: The text content of the file. Use this for text-based assets including HTML, Liquid templates, CSS stylesheets, JavaScript files, JSON config files, and XML. Provide the raw file content as a string. **Constraint**: Exactly one of value, attachment, src, or source_key must be provided.

inputs.name: theme_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier for the theme where the asset will be created or updated. Obtain theme IDs using the GET_THEMES action.

inputs.name: attachment
inputs.about: Base64-encoded binary data for non-text assets such as images (PNG, JPG, GIF, SVG), fonts, or other binary files. The binary file must be encoded in base64 format before sending. **Constraint**: Exactly one of value, attachment, src, or source_key must be provided.

inputs.name: source_key
inputs.about: Path to an existing asset in the same theme to duplicate. Creates a copy of the specified asset at the new location defined by 'key'. Useful for creating backups or template variations. **Constraint**: Exactly one of value, attachment, src, or source_key must be provided.

tools.name: Create Storefront Access Token
tools.description: Creates a new storefront access token for unauthenticated Storefront API access. The token delegates unauthenticated access scopes to clients that need to access the Storefront API without authentication. Requirements: - The app must be configured as an 'extendable' (Sales Channel) app in the Shopify Partner Dashboard - The app must have at least one unauthenticated access scope granted (e.g., unauthenticated_read_product_listings, unauthenticated_write_checkouts) - The created token inherits all unauthenticated scopes from the app Limitations: Maximum 100 active tokens per shop. Tokens cannot be updated after creation, only deleted.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: An arbitrary identifier for the token with no constraint on uniqueness. Used for reference purposes.

tools.name: Create Theme
tools.description: Creates a new theme in Shopify from a ZIP file containing theme assets. Requires a publicly accessible URL to the ZIP file. The theme will default to 'unpublished' status unless the role is explicitly set to 'main' (which publishes the theme immediately after file extraction). Note: This action requires the 'write_themes' scope, which needs merchant approval in Shopify. A store can have a maximum of 20 themes.

inputs.name: src
inputs.about: Publicly accessible URL where Shopify can download the theme ZIP file. The ZIP must contain valid theme files. If not provided, an empty theme will be created.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name to assign to the new theme. This will be displayed in the Shopify admin. Maximum 50 characters.

inputs.name: role
inputs.about: The theme's role/status: 'main' (published and active on store), 'unpublished' (not visible to customers), 'development' (for testing). Defaults to 'unpublished'. WARNING: Setting to 'main' will immediately publish this theme on your live store after file extraction completes.

tools.name: Create Usage Charge
tools.description: Create a variable usage fee against the app's existing recurring charge. Requires a recurring application charge configured with capped_amount and terms. This bills the merchant; for testing use only your own test=true recurring charge. There is no separate test flag for usage charges. Charges exceeding the remaining cap fail. REST Admin API is legacy; new public apps must use GraphQL appUsageRecordCreate instead.

inputs.name: price
inputs.about: Usage charge price in the shop's currency, preferably decimal text (for example, '1.00'). Must not exceed the recurring charge's remaining usage balance.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: Description of the usage charge shown to the merchant.

inputs.name: recurring_application_charge_id
inputs.about: ID of the app's recurring application charge with usage billing enabled.

tools.name: Create Webhook (Deprecated)
tools.description: Creates a new webhook subscription in Shopify to receive real-time notifications when specific events occur in the store. Webhooks allow your application to be notified automatically when events like order creation, product updates, or customer changes happen. The webhook will POST event data to the specified address. Required parameters: address (destination URL) and topic (event type). Optional parameters: format (defaults to 'json'), fields (to limit payload size), metafield_namespaces (to include metafields). Requires 'write_webhooks' scope. May also require topic-specific scopes (e.g., 'read_orders' for orders/* topics).

inputs.name: topic
inputs.about: Event that triggers the webhook. Common topics include: orders/create, orders/updated, products/create, products/update, customers/create, customers/update, app/uninstalled, shop/update, collections/create, inventory_items/update. See Shopify webhook documentation for the complete list of available

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: Optional array of top-level resource fields to serialize and send. If omitted, all fields are included.

inputs.name: format
inputs.about: Data format for webhook delivery. Accepts 'json' or 'xml'. Defaults to 'json' if not specified.

inputs.name: address
inputs.about: Destination URI where the webhook should send POST requests when events occur. Supports standard HTTPS URLs, Google Pub/Sub topics (format: pubsub://projectName:topicName), and Amazon EventBridge ARNs.

inputs.name: metafield_namespaces
inputs.about: Array of metafield namespaces to include with each webhook.

tools.name: Create webhook subscription
tools.description: Create a webhook subscription that notifies your app when specific events occur in a Shopify store. Use when you need real-time event notifications for orders, products, customers, or other resources. Supports HTTPS URLs, Google Pub/Sub topics, and AWS EventBridge event sources.

inputs.name: topic
inputs.about: The type of event that triggers the webhook (e.g., ORDERS_CREATE, PRODUCTS_UPDATE, APP_UNINSTALLED).

inputs.name: webhookSubscription
inputs.about: Webhook subscription configuration object including callback URL and optional filters.

tools.name: Customize Recurring Application Charge
tools.description: Request a new usage-based cap for an active recurring application charge. Only capped_amount can be changed; annual subscriptions are not supported. Return update_capped_amount_url to the merchant for approval; a successful response does not mean the merchant has accepted the new cap. Uses the legacy REST Admin API; Shopify recommends appSubscriptionLineItemUpdate.

inputs.name: capped_amount
inputs.about: New usage-based billing cap in the shop's currency, sent as recurring_application_charge[capped_amount] in the query string.

inputs.name: recurring_application_charge_id
inputs.about: ID of the active recurring application charge to customize.

tools.name: Delete Article
tools.description: Delete an article from a blog in Shopify. Use when you need to permanently remove blog content. This action is irreversible.

inputs.name: blog_id
inputs.about: The ID of the blog containing the article to be deleted.

inputs.name: article_id
inputs.about: The ID of the article to be deleted.

tools.name: Delete a blog
tools.description: Permanently deletes a blog from a Shopify store using its `blog_id`; this action is irreversible and requires the 'content' access scope.

inputs.name: blog_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier for the blog to be deleted. This ID is assigned by Shopify when the blog is created. Can be provided as an integer or string.

tools.name: Delete Carrier Service
tools.description: Permanently remove a carrier service from a Shopify store by its numeric ID. Removes the service used to provide real-time shipping rates at checkout. Requires write_shipping permission and carrier service access on the store. Successful deletion returns an empty JSON object.

inputs.name: carrier_service_id
inputs.about: Numeric ID of the carrier service to permanently delete. Obtain it from a carrier service list or get response.

tools.name: Remove product from collection
tools.description: Removes a product from a custom collection by deleting the collect. Use when you need to unlink a specific product from a custom collection using the collect ID.

inputs.name: collect_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier of the collect to remove. A collect represents the relationship between a specific product and a custom collection. To find collect IDs, use the 'Get collects' action to list all product-collection relationships. Note: This endpoint only works with custom collections, n

tools.name: Remove a comment
tools.description: Remove a comment from a Shopify blog. Use when you need to hide a comment from blog readers while preserving the data. The comment status will be changed to 'removed'. Note: This action requires 'write_content' scope and protected customer data access approval from Shopify, as comments contain customer information (author, email, IP address).

inputs.name: comment_id
inputs.about: The numeric identifier for the comment to be removed. The comment will be marked as removed and hidden from blog readers.

tools.name: Delete country
tools.description: Deletes a country from the shop's tax configuration. Removes a country that was previously added to the shop's tax settings. The country must have been added via the API or Shopify admin for this operation to succeed. Requires the 'write_shipping' scope. DEPRECATION WARNING: This REST API endpoint was deprecated in API version 2024-07 (effective July 1, 2024). The recommended alternative is the GraphQL Countries in Shipping Zone API. This endpoint may not be available in newer API versions or may have restricted access in many Shopify stores.

inputs.name: country_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier (as a string) for the country to be removed from the shop's tax configuration. This ID can be obtained from the GET countries endpoint.

tools.name: Delete custom collection (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use SHOPIFY_DELETES_A_CUSTOM_COLLECTION instead. Permanently deletes a custom collection from a Shopify store using its `collection_id`; this action is irreversible and requires a valid, existing `collection_id`.

inputs.name: collection_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the custom collection that needs to be deleted. This ID is a numerical string assigned by Shopify when the collection is created.

tools.name: Delete a customer
tools.description: Deletes a customer from the Shopify store. Use when you need to permanently remove a customer who has no existing orders. Cannot delete customers with existing orders.

inputs.name: customer_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the customer to be deleted. Note: A customer cannot be deleted if they have existing orders.

tools.name: Delete customer address
tools.description: Removes an address from a customer's address list. Cannot delete the customer's default address - to delete a default address, first assign a different address as the default.

inputs.name: address_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the address to be removed from the customer's address list. Note: Cannot delete the customer's default address without first assigning a different address as default.

inputs.name: customer_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the customer whose address will be deleted.

tools.name: Delete dispute evidence file
tools.description: Delete an uploaded evidence file from a Shopify Payments dispute. Requires Shopify-approved write_shopify_payments_dispute_file_uploads access. Uses the legacy REST Admin API; new public apps must use GraphQL. Returns an empty result for the documented successful response.

inputs.name: dispute_id
inputs.about: Numeric Shopify Payments dispute ID.

inputs.name: dispute_file_upload_id
inputs.about: Numeric ID of the dispute evidence file to delete.

tools.name: Delete a draft order
tools.description: Delete a draft order from Shopify. Use when you need to remove an existing draft order permanently.

inputs.name: draft_order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the draft order to delete. This ID is required to target the correct draft order for removal.

tools.name: Delete fulfillment event
tools.description: Deletes a fulfillment event (tracking status update) from an order's fulfillment. Use this action when you need to remove an incorrect or outdated tracking event from a fulfillment. Fulfillment events represent tracking status updates like 'in_transit', 'out_for_delivery', or 'delivered' that are displayed to customers on the order status page. Common use cases: - Removing duplicate tracking events - Correcting erroneous status updates - Cleaning up test events Prerequisites: You must have valid order_id, fulfillment_id, and event_id. These can be obtained from order retrieval actions or fulfillment event list actions. Note: This REST endpoint is deprecated. For new integrations, consider using the GraphQL Admin API. Requires 'write_orders' scope and approval for protected customer data access.

inputs.name: event_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier for the fulfillment event to delete. You can obtain this from fulfillment event retrieval actions (e.g., get_fulfillment_events) or from the event.id field when creating fulfillment events.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier for the order. You can obtain this from order retrieval actions (e.g., list_order, get_order) or from the order.id field in order objects.

inputs.name: fulfillment_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier for the fulfillment within the order. You can obtain this from the fulfillments array in an order object (e.g., order.fulfillments[0].id) or from fulfillment creation/retrieval actions.

tools.name: Remove fulfillment service
tools.description: Remove an existing fulfillment service from a Shopify store. Use when you need to permanently delete a third-party fulfillment service.

inputs.name: fulfillment_service_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the fulfillment service to remove. This is the numeric ID of the fulfillment service you want to delete.

tools.name: Delete inventory levels
tools.description: Deletes an inventory level of an inventory item at a location. Deleting an inventory level removes that item from the specified location. Every inventory item must have at least one inventory level.

inputs.name: location_id
inputs.about: The ID of the location that the inventory level belongs to. To find the ID of the location, use the Location resource.

inputs.name: inventory_item_id
inputs.about: The ID for the inventory item. This identifies the specific inventory item to remove from the location.

tools.name: Delete a marketing event
tools.description: Delete a marketing event from Shopify. Use when you need to remove an existing marketing event from the system.

inputs.name: marketing_event_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the marketing event to delete. This ID is required to target the specific marketing event for removal.

tools.name: Delete a metafield by its ID
tools.description: Deletes a metafield by its ID from any Shopify resource. Use this action to permanently remove metafields from: - Shop-level metafields (use resource='shop' or 'metafields') - Product metafields (resource='products') - Collection metafields (resource='collections') - Customer metafields (resource='customers') - Order metafields (resource='orders') - Other resource-specific metafields The deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. Returns an empty response on success.

inputs.name: resource
inputs.about: The resource type that owns the metafield. Use 'shop' or 'metafields' for shop-level metafields. Use specific resource types like 'products', 'customers', 'orders', 'collections', 'blogs', etc. for resource-specific metafields.

inputs.name: resource_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the parent resource that owns the metafield. This parameter is required but ignored for shop-level metafields (when resource is 'shop' or 'metafields'). For other resource types, provide the actual resource ID.

inputs.name: metafield_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the metafield to delete. This is the metafield's ID, not the owner resource ID.

tools.name: Delete metaobject
tools.description: Deletes a metaobject and its associated metafields using GraphQL mutation. Use when you need to permanently remove a metaobject from the Shopify store. The deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the metaobject to delete. Must be a Shopify GID in the format 'gid://shopify/Metaobject/{id}' or just the numeric ID.

tools.name: Delete metaobject definition
tools.description: Delete a metaobject definition and all its associated data. Use when you need to completely remove a metaobject definition schema. This mutation also asynchronously deletes all related metafield definitions, metaobjects, and metafields.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the metaobject definition to delete. Must be in the format: gid://shopify/MetaobjectDefinition/{id} where {id} is the numeric ID. This mutation also deletes all related metafield definitions, metaobjects, and metafields asynchronously.

tools.name: Delete Mobile Platform Application
tools.description: Permanently delete a mobile platform application association by its ID. Removes the Shopify association, not the installed iOS or Android app. Requires the mobile_platform_applications scope, which Shopify Support must enable for the app. Uses the legacy REST Admin API. Returns an empty object.

inputs.name: mobile_platform_application_id
inputs.about: Numeric ID of the mobile platform application to permanently delete, supplied as a string. Obtain it from a list or get response.

tools.name: Delete an order
tools.description: Permanently delete an order from Shopify. Use when you need to remove test orders, orders paid with manual payment methods, or draft orders marked as paid. Orders must be archived or canceled before deletion. Orders that interact with an online gateway, are paid via Shopify POS, online checkout, or with gift cards cannot be deleted.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Shopify order to delete. Orders that interact with an online gateway cannot be deleted. The order must be archived or canceled before deletion.

tools.name: Delete order risk
tools.description: Requests deletion of an order risk by order ID and risk ID using the configured Shopify REST API version. This deprecated action can delete only risks created by the application.

inputs.name: risk_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the order risk to be removed. Note: You can only delete an order risk that was created by your application - risks created by other applications cannot be deleted.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the order containing the risk to be deleted.

tools.name: Delete a page
tools.description: Delete a page from a Shopify store permanently. Use when you need to remove an existing page; this operation is irreversible and requires content access scope.

inputs.name: page_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier for the page to be deleted. This can be obtained from page listing endpoints or page creation responses. The deletion is permanent and irreversible.

tools.name: Delete price rule
tools.description: Deletes an existing price rule from the Shopify store permanently. Use this action to remove price rules that are no longer needed. Note that deleting a price rule will also delete any discount codes associated with it. This operation is idempotent - deleting an already-deleted price rule will return an error. Common use cases: - Removing expired or outdated promotional campaigns - Cleaning up test price rules from development - Deactivating seasonal sales or limited-time offers To get a price rule ID: use the list price rules action or reference the ID from when you created the price rule.

inputs.name: price_rule_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the price rule to delete. You can obtain price rule IDs by listing price rules or from the response when creating a price rule.

tools.name: Delete a product
tools.description: Permanently deletes a product from a Shopify store by its product ID. This action is irreversible - deleted products cannot be recovered. Deleting a product also removes all associated variants, images, inventory, and removes the product from all collections and sales channels store-wide. If the goal is collection-only cleanup, adjust collection membership instead.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier of the product to delete. You can obtain this ID from product creation responses or by listing products. Example: '8313381814466' Must be a numeric REST ID (e.g., '8313381814466'); GraphQL GID formats (e.g., 'gid://shopify/Product/123') are not accepted.

tools.name: Delete product image
tools.description: Deletes a specific image from a product in Shopify, requiring the `product_id` of an existing product and the `image_id` of an image currently associated with that product.

inputs.name: image_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the specific product image to be deleted.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the product from which the image is to be deleted.

tools.name: Delete product metafield
tools.description: Deletes a specific Shopify product metafield using the product ID and metafield ID. A not-found response is returned in userErrors rather than raised as an HTTP error.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Shopify product.

inputs.name: metafield_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the metafield to delete. Deletion is permanent and irreversible. Verify the correct metafield by checking its namespace, key, and value before deletion, as multiple metafields can share similar keys across different namespaces.

tools.name: Remove product variant
tools.description: Deletes a specific product variant from a Shopify store using its unique product ID and variant ID; this action is irreversible. Use when you need to permanently remove a variant from a product.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Shopify product that contains the variant to be deleted.

inputs.name: variant_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the specific product variant to be deleted.

tools.name: Delete redirect
tools.description: Permanently deletes a URL redirect from a Shopify store. Use this tool to remove redirect rules that are no longer needed. A redirect automatically forwards visitors from an old URL path to a new target location. When you delete a redirect, visitors to the old path will no longer be automatically forwarded. Note: This operation is destructive and cannot be undone. If the redirect ID doesn't exist, the API will return a 404 error.

inputs.name: redirect_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier of the redirect to delete. You can obtain redirect IDs by listing redirects or from redirect creation responses.

tools.name: Delete a custom collection
tools.description: Permanently delete a custom collection from a Shopify store. Use when you need to remove a custom collection that is no longer needed. This operation is irreversible and requires the 'write_products' access scope.

inputs.name: custom_collection_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the custom collection to be deleted. This ID is included in the URL path.

tools.name: Delete a discount code
tools.description: Delete a discount code from a price rule. Use when you need to remove a specific discount code associated with a price rule.

inputs.name: price_rule_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the price rule associated with the discount code. You can obtain price rule IDs by listing price rules using the 'Get Price Rules List' action or by creating a price rule.

inputs.name: discount_code_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the discount code to delete. You can obtain discount code IDs by listing discount codes for a price rule using the 'Get Discount Codes' action.

tools.name: Delete a saved search
tools.description: Delete a saved search in Shopify. Use when you need to remove a saved search by its ID. The ID must be provided in GID format (gid://shopify/SavedSearch/[ID]).

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the saved search to delete. Must be in GID format: gid://shopify/SavedSearch/[ID]. Example: gid://shopify/SavedSearch/123456789

tools.name: Delete Script Tag
tools.description: Delete a script tag from your Shopify store. Permanently removes a script tag using its unique identifier. Script tags are JavaScript files that load on your storefront. Use this action to clean up deprecated scripts or remove third-party integrations. Requires 'write_script_tags' OAuth scope. Common use cases: - Remove outdated analytics or tracking scripts - Clean up after uninstalling third-party apps - Delete test scripts from development Note: Script tags are automatically deleted when the app that created them is uninstalled.

inputs.name: script_tag_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier of the script tag to delete. Obtain this ID from list/get script tag endpoints.

tools.name: Delete smart collection
tools.description: Permanently removes a smart collection from a Shopify store using its `smart_collection_id`; this action is irreversible and requires a valid, existing smart collection ID.

inputs.name: smart_collection_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the smart collection to be deleted. This ID is a numerical string assigned by Shopify when the smart collection is created.

tools.name: Delete Storefront Access Token
tools.description: Delete an existing storefront access token from a Shopify store. Use when you need to permanently revoke access for a storefront access token. This operation is irreversible.

inputs.name: storefront_access_token_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the storefront access token to delete. This is the numeric ID of the token.

tools.name: Delete theme
tools.description: Deletes a Shopify theme by ID using the write_themes scope. Deleted theme details may be returned, but a successful empty response contains no theme details.

inputs.name: theme_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier for the theme to delete. Can be obtained from GET /themes.json endpoint or from the theme's admin_graphql_api_id (extract the numeric portion). Must be a valid, existing theme ID.

tools.name: Delete theme asset
tools.description: Delete an asset from a Shopify theme. Use when you need to remove a specific asset file (such as CSS, JavaScript, images, or template files) from a theme by providing the theme ID and asset key. Note that required theme assets like layout/theme.liquid cannot be deleted and will result in an error.

inputs.name: theme_id
inputs.about: The ID of the theme containing the asset to delete.

inputs.name: asset_key
inputs.about: The key representing the asset's path within the theme to delete (e.g., 'assets/bg-body.gif', 'templates/index.liquid'). Maximum 100 characters.

tools.name: Delete webhook subscription (Deprecated)
tools.description: Delete a webhook subscription from Shopify. Use when you need to remove an existing webhook. Only the app that registered the webhook can delete it; attempting to delete another app's webhook will return a 404 error.

inputs.name: webhook_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier of the webhook subscription to delete. Only the app that registered the webhook can delete it.

tools.name: Delete webhook subscription
tools.description: Delete a webhook subscription and stop all future webhooks to its endpoint. Use when you need to remove a webhook subscription that is no longer needed. Returns the deleted subscription's ID for confirmation. Note: If you only use app-specific webhooks, this may not be needed. App-specific webhook subscriptions in shopify.app.toml are automatically managed by Shopify.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the webhook subscription to delete. Must be in the format gid://shopify/WebhookSubscription/{id}. This is the globally unique identifier (GID) for the webhook subscription, not the numeric ID.

tools.name: Delete web presence
tools.description: Delete a web presence from Shopify. Use when you need to remove a web presence by its ID.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the web presence to delete. Must be in the format gid://shopify/WebPresence/{numeric_id} or just the numeric ID.

tools.name: Disable a Gift Card
tools.description: Disable a gift card in Shopify. Use when you need to permanently deactivate a gift card. WARNING: This operation is irreversible and the gift card cannot be re-enabled once disabled.

inputs.name: gift_card_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the gift card to disable. This operation is irreversible and cannot be undone.

tools.name: Enable standard metaobject definition
tools.description: Enable a standard metaobject definition from its template. Use when you need to activate a predefined Shopify metaobject template for use in your store.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The type of the standard metaobject definition to enable. This is a predefined template type provided by Shopify (e.g., 'product_review').

tools.name: Get abandonment
tools.description: Retrieves an abandonment record from Shopify using its unique ID. Use when you need to query customer abandonment data including type, customer info, email state, and timing details.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the abandonment in GID format (e.g., 'gid://shopify/Abandonment/1').

tools.name: Get abandonment by abandoned checkout ID
tools.description: Query abandonment information by abandoned checkout ID using Shopify's GraphQL Admin API. Use when you need to retrieve customer journey data, abandonment type, and email state for a specific abandoned checkout. Returns null if the checkout doesn't exist or has no abandonment tracking.

inputs.name: abandoned_checkout_id
inputs.about: The ID of the abandoned checkout to query. Must be in Shopify GID format (e.g., 'gid://shopify/AbandonedCheckout/12345') or a numeric ID that will be converted to GID format.

tools.name: Get a list of access scopes
tools.description: Retrieves a list of access scopes associated with the access token. Use when you need to view the permissions that merchants have granted during app installation.

tools.name: Get App
tools.description: Query information about a Shopify app using the GraphQL API. Use when you need to retrieve details about the currently authenticated app or a specific app by its ID.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the app to retrieve. Must be in the format gid://shopify/App/{ID}. If omitted, returns the currently authenticated app.

tools.name: Get app by handle
tools.description: Query app information by handle using the Shopify Admin GraphQL API. Use when you need to retrieve details about a specific Shopify app using its handle.

inputs.name: handle
inputs.about: Handle of the App - a URL-friendly identifier (e.g., 'shopify-flow', 'product-reviews').

tools.name: Get app installation details
tools.description: Query a specific app installation on a Shopify store. Use when you need to retrieve details about an app installation including access scopes, launch URL, and uninstall URL.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the AppInstallation to retrieve. If omitted, returns the AppInstallation for the currently authenticated app.

tools.name: Get Application Charge By ID
tools.description: Retrieve a single application charge by its unique identifier. Use when you need detailed information about a specific one-time charge.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the application charge to retrieve.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of fields to include in the response (e.g., 'id,name,price,status'). By default, all fields are returned.

tools.name: Get Application Charges
tools.description: Retrieves a list of one-time application charges for the current app installation. Application charges are one-time fees charged to merchants for app usage. This endpoint returns all charges with their status (pending, accepted, active, declined, expired). Use this to monitor billing history, verify charge status, or implement pagination with since_id. Returns an empty list if no charges exist, which is normal for new app installations.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of fields to include in the response (e.g., 'id,name,price,status'). By default, all fields are returned.

inputs.name: since_id
inputs.about: Retrieve only application charges with an ID greater than this specified ID. This is used for paginating through results.

tools.name: Get application credit
tools.description: Retrieve a single application credit issued to a shop by your app. Requires an existing credit ID and an app that uses Shopify's Billing API. Uses the legacy REST Admin API. The provider's creation deprecation does not deprecate this read endpoint. This action does not create financial credits.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of fields to include in the response. By default, all fields are returned.

inputs.name: application_credit_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the application credit issued by your app.

tools.name: Get application credits
tools.description: Retrieve all application credits for a shop. Use when you need to view credits issued to merchants that can be used towards future app purchases.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of fields to include in the response (e.g., 'id,amount,description,test,currency'). By default, all fields are returned.

tools.name: Get Article
tools.description: Retrieves a single article from a Shopify blog by its ID. Use this action when you need to: - Get detailed information about a specific blog article - Retrieve article content, metadata, or publication status - Access article properties like title, author, tags, or images The optional 'fields' parameter allows you to retrieve only specific article properties, reducing response size and improving performance when you don't need the full article data. Requires the 'read_content' OAuth scope.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of article fields to include in the response. Use this to retrieve only specific fields and reduce payload size. Example: 'id,title,author' returns only those three fields.

inputs.name: blog_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier (ID) of the blog containing the article.

inputs.name: article_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier (ID) of the article to retrieve.

tools.name: Get Batch Discount Codes
tools.description: Retrieves discount codes from a batch creation job, showing which succeeded and which failed. **Workflow:** After batch job completes (status='completed'), use this to get the actual codes. 1. Create price rule (get price_rule_id) 2. Create batch job (get batch_id) 3. Poll until completed 4. Use this action to retrieve codes **Response:** Successful codes have id populated and errors={}. Failed codes have id=null and errors with validation details. **Use Cases:** Verify created codes, identify validation errors, get IDs for further operations. **Note:** Requires 'read_price_rules' scope. Max 100 codes per batch.

inputs.name: batch_id
inputs.about: The ID of the batch discount code creation job. Get this from the 'id' field in the response when creating a batch via POST /price_rules/{price_rule_id}/batch.json or from polling GET /price_rules/{price_rule_id}/batch/{batch_id}.json.

inputs.name: price_rule_id
inputs.about: The ID of the price rule associated with the batch discount code creation job. Get this from creating or listing price rules.

tools.name: Get Single Blog
tools.description: Retrieve a single blog by its unique identifier. Use when you need to access detailed information about a specific blog in the Shopify store.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of specific blog properties to include in the response (e.g., 'id,title,handle'). If not specified, all properties are returned.

inputs.name: blog_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier for the blog to retrieve.

tools.name: Get blog article tags
tools.description: Retrieve a list of all article tags from a specific blog. Use when you need to get all unique tags that have been applied to articles in a particular blog, optionally sorted by popularity.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: The maximum number of tags to retrieve. If not specified, all tags are returned.

inputs.name: blog_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the blog to retrieve article tags from.

inputs.name: popular
inputs.about: A flag for ordering retrieved tags by popularity. If present (set to any value like 1), results are ordered by popularity, starting with the most popular tag. If not present, tags are returned in default order.

tools.name: Get bulk operation status
tools.description: Query the status and details of a Shopify bulk operation by its ID. Use when you need to check the progress, status, or results of a previously initiated bulk operation. Returns metadata including status, completion time, result URLs, and error information if applicable. Note: The bulkOperation query requires API version 2025-10 or later.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the BulkOperation to return in GID format (e.g., 'gid://shopify/BulkOperation/6117019975874'). This is the unique identifier for the bulk operation created by bulkOperationRunQuery mutation.

tools.name: Get carrier service
tools.description: Retrieve a single carrier service by ID to inspect its shipping-rate configuration. Uses the legacy Shopify REST Admin API. Unlike the list endpoint, this endpoint retrieves a specific service rather than listing active services.

inputs.name: carrier_service_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the carrier service to retrieve.

tools.name: Get carrier services
tools.description: Retrieves all active carrier services configured in a Shopify store. Carrier services allow apps to provide real-time shipping rates at checkout. This endpoint returns only carrier services where active=true. Requirements: - Store must be on Advanced Shopify plan or higher, OR - Store must be on Shopify plan with yearly billing (with carrier service feature), OR - Store must be a development store Use this to view active carrier services for shipping rate calculations.

tools.name: Get catalogs count
tools.description: Query the count of catalogs in the Shopify store. Use when you need to know how many catalogs exist, optionally filtered by type or search query.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: Enum for catalog type values.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: A filter made up of terms for searching catalogs. Filterable fields: app_id, company_id, company_location_id, id, managed_country_id, market_id, status, title. Example: 'status:ACTIVE'

tools.name: Get checkout payment
tools.description: Retrieve an existing checkout payment by checkout token and payment ID. Returns payment, transaction, card, and checkout details, including nullable processing and authentication information. Requires elevated sales-channel payment processing access and protected customer data approval. Uses the legacy REST Admin API; this action does not create or charge a payment.

inputs.name: token
inputs.about: Token of the existing checkout: URL-safe letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.

inputs.name: payment_id
inputs.about: ID of an existing payment on that checkout.

tools.name: Get checkout profile
tools.description: Retrieves a checkout profile from Shopify using its unique ID. Use when you need to query checkout profile details including name, publication status, and timestamps.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the checkout profile in GID format (e.g., 'gid://shopify/CheckoutProfile/691503298').

tools.name: Get checkouts count
tools.description: Retrieve a count of abandoned checkouts from the past 90 days, optionally filtered by date ranges or status. A 403 response is returned as a count of zero, so zero can also indicate denied access.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Count checkouts with a given status. Default is 'open' if not specified

inputs.name: since_id
inputs.about: Restrict results to after the specified ID

inputs.name: created_at_max
inputs.about: Count checkouts created before the specified date in ISO 8601 format

inputs.name: created_at_min
inputs.about: Count checkouts created after the specified date in ISO 8601 format

inputs.name: updated_at_max
inputs.about: Count checkouts last updated before the specified date in ISO 8601 format

inputs.name: updated_at_min
inputs.about: Count checkouts last updated after the specified date in ISO 8601 format

tools.name: Get collect by ID
tools.description: Retrieves a specific collect by its ID. Use when you need to get details about a specific product-collection relationship.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of fields to retrieve (e.g., 'id,collection_id,product_id'). If omitted, all fields are returned.

inputs.name: collect_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the collect resource. A collect represents the relationship between a product and a custom collection.

tools.name: Get collection by ID
tools.description: Retrieves a specific Shopify collection by its `collection_id`, optionally filtering returned data to specified `fields`.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of fields to retrieve. Note: The Shopify collections endpoint may not fully support field filtering and might return all fields regardless of this parameter. E.g., 'id,title,handle'.

inputs.name: collection_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric identifier of the Shopify collection to retrieve. Must be a numeric ID, not a GraphQL GID.

tools.name: Get collection by identifier
tools.description: Query a collection by identifier (ID or handle) using the Shopify GraphQL Admin API. Use when you need to fetch collection details by either its global ID or unique handle.

inputs.name: identifier
inputs.about: The identifier used to fetch the collection. Must provide either id or handle field.

tools.name: Get collection listing
tools.description: Retrieve a specific collection listing published to your sales channel app. Uses the legacy REST Admin API. Requires a collection listing visible to the current app and merchant-approved read_product_listings access. Publishing a collection does not automatically publish its products to your channel.

inputs.name: collection_listing_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID of the collection listing to retrieve.

tools.name: Get collects
tools.description: Retrieves a list of collects from a Shopify store, where a collect links a product to a custom collection. Returns only collect mapping records (collect_id, collection_id, product_id, position, etc.), not full product details — use SHOPIFY_GET_PRODUCTS_IN_COLLECTION if product details are needed.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Maximum number of collects to retrieve (1-250).

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: Comma-separated list of fields to retrieve (e.g., `id,collection_id,product_id`); if unspecified, all fields are returned.

inputs.name: since_id
inputs.about: Retrieve only collects created after this ID, for pagination.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: Filter collects by product ID to retrieve only collections that contain a specific product.

inputs.name: collection_id
inputs.about: Filter collects by custom collection ID to retrieve only products linked to a specific collection.

tools.name: Get collects count
tools.description: Retrieves a count of collects (product-collection relationships). Use when you need to know the total number of collects, optionally filtered by collection_id or product_id.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: Filter counts to a specific product. Returns only collects for this product.

inputs.name: collection_id
inputs.about: Filter counts to a specific custom collection. Returns only collects belonging to this collection.

tools.name: Get Comment
tools.description: Retrieve a single article comment by ID using the legacy REST Admin API. Returns comment content, author information and moderation status. Use fields to select specific properties. Requires read_content (or write_content) and protected customer data access.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: Comma-separated comment fields to include, such as 'id,body,author'.

inputs.name: comment_id
inputs.about: The positive numeric ID of the comment to retrieve.

tools.name: Get count of comments
tools.description: Retrieves a count of comments. Use when you need to know how many comments exist, optionally filtered by article, blog, status, or date ranges.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Filter results by their status. Options: pending, published, unapproved.

inputs.name: blog_id
inputs.about: Identifier for the blog containing articles to count comments from.

inputs.name: article_id
inputs.about: Identifier for the specific article whose comments to count.

inputs.name: created_at_max
inputs.about: Count comments created before this date in ISO 8601 format.

inputs.name: created_at_min
inputs.about: Count comments created after this date in ISO 8601 format.

inputs.name: updated_at_max

tools.name: Execute Shopify GraphQL query
tools.description: Executes a GraphQL query against the Shopify Admin API for flexible data retrieval and mutations including metafields. Response data is nested under result['data']['data'], not result['data']. Always inspect both response_data.errors (top-level) and mutation-level userErrors—HTTP 200 can accompany GraphQL validation failures. Query costs draw from a ~1000-point bucket (~50 points/second refill); monitor extensions.cost.throttleStatus to avoid THROTTLED errors. Paginate list queries using pageInfo.hasNextPage and endCursor to avoid silently missing records. productUpdate replaces the entire tags array—send the complete final tag list. refundCreate requires orderId at both the top level and inside each transactions element. transaction parentId must reference a CAPTURE-kind transaction. Numeric fields like numberOfOrders may be returned as strings—cast before aggregating.
